de70eead-6ace-46ed-a9f9-a8c082e5a36d: Join us on Tuesday, December 1 when we welcome Jen Siraganian for the release of her debut poetry collection, Everything Has Been Moved, Even the Dead, at 9th Ave Featuring Tongo Eisen-Martin, Nancy Miller Gomez, and Christin Rice Presented in partnership with Litquake Free to Attend, Please RSVP Or Watch on YouTube Live/Link Available Soon Proceeds from this event benefit Doctors Without Borders. Donate with your RSVP or directly at their website. About Everything Has Been Moved, Even the Dead In her debut collection, Everything Has Been Moved, Even the Dead, Jen Siraganian traces a self shaped by history, fragmentation, and memory as she weaves her family’s past in the Middle East with her identity as an Armenian-American woman and mother. Whether portraying a grandparent’s survival during the Armenian Genocide, a father’s childhood in 1940s Palestine, or a son’s birth when “death is a neighbor,” Siraganian’s poems interrogate concepts of home, origins, belonging, and displacement. Using a docupoetic lens, the poet braids narratives with archival photographs and artifacts to chart cycles of cultural and historic erasure while enacting an intertextual conversation with artists of the diaspora, and with art itself. Through poems that seed each other with recurring images of pomegranates, mushrooms, and fire, Everything Has Been Moved, Even the Dead pushes against annihilation with a voice that resists silence. About Jen Siraganian Jen Siraganian is an Armenian-American writer, educator, and former poet laureate of Los Gatos, California. Her poetry has appeared in AGNI, Best New Poets 2016 and 2025, The Cincinnati Review, Electric Literature, Poetry Daily, Prairie Schooner, The Rumpus, the anthology Heaven Looks Like Us: Palestinian Poetry, and elsewhere, and she is a winner of the New Ohio Review Poetry Prize and The Writing Salon’s Jane Underwood Poetry Prize, She served as managing director of Litquake: San Francisco’s Literary Festival, and she is a Lucas Artist Fellow at the Montalvo Arts Center in Saratoga, California. Everything Has Been Moved, Even the Dead is her first book.

a640e76d-f6bc-4f95-ba90-97531b14949a: From an acclaimed New York Times bestselling biographer comes a remarkable new look at the only man to serve as both president and chief justice of the United States. The conventional wisdom is that William Howard Taft was a mediocre president, a man almost without political skills. Yet Taft’s modest, judicial approach to the presidency—he served as a state and then federal judge before entering the White House—looks quite extraordinary in retrospect. Admired by those on either side of the aisle for his genial personality and hearty chuckle, Taft spent his four years in office reducing tariffs, eliminating federal deficits, pursuing government efficiency, avoiding foreign wars, and honoring the Constitution. Yet even Taft’s presidency would serve as merely a prelude to one of the greatest second acts in American history. More than any chief justice since John Marshall, Taft transformed the judicial branch, particularly as the principal proponent of the legislation that allowed the Supreme Court to begin choosing its cases—and thus to devote its energy entirely to deciding key constitutional and statutory issues. A rigorously researched and elegant account of five decades of public service, William Howard Taft offers a bold reassessment of a forgotten great American. Walter Stahr is the New York Times bestselling author of Seward: Lincoln’s Indispensable Man , Stanton: Lincoln’s War Secretary , and John Jay: Founding Father . A two-time winner of the Seward Award for Excellence in Civil War Biography, Stahr practiced law in Washington and Asia for more than two decades. An honors graduate of Stanford University and Harvard Law School, he now lives in Newport Beach, California. c6c322d7-7bbb-4dd3-8608-7fa378f6a229: Rebecca Handler the award-winning author of Edie Richter is Not Alone presents her profoundly moving new novel, In the Round . "Only Rebecca Handler can write a play within a novel within an identity crisis that comes with cat jokes, an extraordinary act of kindness, betrayal, and disdain for musical theater . In The Round is profound and pithy and not like any other book you will ever read in just one sitting. Wow." —Marcy Dermansky Rebecca will be joined in conversation by Daniel Handler. A woman is consumed by the belief that her life has become a play. Lively, moving, and at moments astonishing, Rebecca Handler’s Kafkaesque literary mystery is either a reflection on middle-aged malaise or the cover-up for a murderous plot. Or maybe it’s a theatrical production. We meet In the Round’s unnamed protagonist a few minutes after she’s become convinced she’s a victim of a home invasion. Nothing is missing from her family’s San Francisco home, but everything feels wrong. Certain a burglar was there recently, the woman lurks about her own house during a sleepless night of questioning. Have you ever been sure that someone is watching you? Does a lifetime of putting others first lead to permanent paranoia? Have we all built versions of ourselves we’re performing for an unseen audience? In the depths of one strange night in her living room, she seeks answers from her teenage son and her troubled neighbor. She dances to ’90s music and buys herself underwear online. And she wonders: Will she be able to solve the mystery of her own purpose so she can save herself? “I read the opening pages of this remarkable book with a thrill of finding myself in the hands of a gifted conjuror, and finished in a state of total enchantment, profoundly moved.” —Michael Chabon "In this delicately immersive novel, quiet shifts of scale, reminiscent of the great Paula Fox, evoke a whole sense of our time. Here, the dynamics of witnessing and surveillance are the constant texture of consciousness. Mapping the movements of the mind of an ordinary woman at home in the night, Rebecca Handler shows us what makes a life worth watching: access to the everyday endurance of suffering and the reality of joy." —Lucy Corin "What a beguiling storyteller Rebecca Handler is! In the Round gives the readers an enthralling pleasure of being inside a character and watching the character from outside, which is perhaps akin to the most important experience of living with attention and reflection." —Yiyun Li "I wandered into this literary labyrinth late at night, thinking I'll just take a quick peek at what's inside. Instead, I found myself forgoing sleep to follow its twists and turns, surprised and delighted, reluctant to return to the real world." —Soma Mei-Sheng Frazier " In the Round is the most exciting, original novel I've read in years. I couldn't put it down and couldn't stop thinking about it long after I'd read the breathtaking final words. Fans of Katie Kitamura, Jenny Offill, and Rachel Cusk: Here is your new favorite writer." —Joanna Rakoff "I read the spectacular IN THE ROUND in a single delighted sitting, entranced by the possibilities opened up, the life made urgent and real. Bravissima!" —R. O. Kwon Rebecca Handler’s debut novel, Edie Richter is Not Alone , received a Kirkus Starred Review and was longlisted for the Center for Fiction First Novel Prize. Her short stories have been published and awarded in several anthologies. A MacDowell fellow, Rebecca lives in San Francisco with her husband and, when they’re not off pursuing their own adventures, their two daughters. 13fd233f-176b-4b6c-b9c9-e9eaf3cb244e: Implosions and Injustice in San Francisco · Marie Harrison (1948-2019), an environmental activist of San Francisco’s Bayview Hunters Point, spent her life fighting for basic services such as housing, energy, and employment that had become money makers for a few but a dream deferred for her community. What she endured, from the brown water that ran out of her taps at Geneva Towers, the blood that ran from her grandson’s nose while living next door to the PG&E smokestacks, and the fear of radiation poisoning from one of the country’s worst superfund cleanup sites, are environmental injustices that citizens of the United States suffer every day. Freelance journalist Tom Molanphy will be in conversation with Arieann Harrison , ennvironmental activist and Marie's daughter, about Marie's life, legacy, and the continued fight for environmental justice. Half of the book proceeds will go to the Marie Harrison Community Foundation . Tom Molanphy ’s journalism has appeared in 48 Hills, USA Today Travel.com, Earth Island Journal, and The San Francisco Chronicle , among other publications. His work as a 2022 USC Annenberg Center for Health Journalism Data Fellow led to a 2023 1st Place Award in Environmental Reporting from the California News Publishers Association. His essay “The Road Less: John Huston, Blue-Footed Boobies and Me” earned a 2017 Bay Area Travel Writers award, and his short story “Of Subareas and Public Bathrooms” was included in the California Prose Directory. His last book was a memoir, Loud Memories Of A Quiet Life . He is a member of the Society of Environmental Journalists and teaches journalism, composition, creative writing and art/design appreciation classes at the Academy of Art University in San Francisco. Arieann Harrison is the Founder and Executive Director of the Marie Harrison Community Foundation . Arieann Harrison is a resident of San Francisco District 10 and has lived and worked in the Bayview Community for 30+ years. Her work includes providing social services, employment opportunities, community resources, and engaging in environmental advocacy with local D10 residents, taking an all-inclusive, solutions-based approach to providing good information for the best outcome that will lead to preservation of life. #CanWeLive has become the rallying cry of a community that has gone long overlooked when it comes to social, environmental, and economic justice.

What is Sutro Tower actually for? What's the real story behind Coit Tower? And how did a grand Roman-style rotunda end up next to a lagoon in the Marina? df9e3abe-56e2-459d-a721-4205e3138ce1: For nearly two thousand years, the Eleusinian Mysteries initiated tens of thousands of people annually into a shared encounter with death, dissolution, and return. Ancient Greek mystery cults were complete ritual architectures, sophisticated enough to hold those tens of thousands of initiates annually, persisting across empires and political orders. When Eleusis was dismantled by imperial edict in 392 CE, what was lost was not the sacrament alone, but the ritual container, the community, and the cosmological framework that gave the experience meaning, that enabled the initiate to return to the world transformed, and to have that transformation recognized by the community. We are living through a moment of profound planetary transformation. The current Western appetite for plant medicines, indigenous wisdom, and the ancient Greek mysteries is not coincidental but a symptom of the need for our current spiritual and ontological structures to uphold meaning in times of crisis, but that modernity has left unmaintained. Society needs initiatory ritual to face death, dissolution, and all those experiences that exceed the bounds of language and the canonical pillars of civic and economic order. Eleana Baskouta and Nikos Katsaounis present a two-part evening: the deep history and living ritual ecologies of the ancient Mediterranean mystery traditions, the contemporary archaeo-pharmacological research on the kykeon beverage at the heart of the ritual, and an open conversation on what the demand for initiatory containers in an age of polycrisis actually requires. What would a modern mystery institution adequate to our era look like? Please purchase your ticket in advance, as we cannot guarantee entry for walk-ins. We recommend arriving 15 minutes early to allow time for check-in and settling in. Eleana is a Greek interdisciplinary scholar, AMFT and philanthropy advisor who works across sectors to design collaborative research ecosystems, mobilize capital and develop partnerships that bridge scientific inquiry with cultural and historical insight. She is co-founder and Partnership Lead of EPOPTEIA — the Hellenic Center for Entheogenic Research — a research institute that investigates the ethnobotanical and pharmacological heritage of ancient Greek ritual pharmaka. She holds an MA in Integral Psychotherapy from the California Institute of Integral Studies, an MA in Development Economics and International Relations from the Fletcher School at Tufts University, and a BA in Cultural Anthropology from the National University of Athens. She began her career in development research and strategy in Europe before transitioning into major gifts fundraising and partnership development for educational and research institutions in the US. At EPOPTEIA, Eleana oversees partnership development, strategic planning, and philanthropic engagement. Nikos Katsaounis is a Greek-born filmmaker, media entrepreneur and systems thinker who has spent two decades building contemporary rooms for very old experiences. He co-directed Entheogen: Awakening the Divine Within (2006), a documentary on techno-shamanism, electronic dance culture and the revival of initiatory rites, featuring Terence McKenna. His film and media work has earned Emmy and Webby awards. dab69eb9-a5da-4d15-b123-b7d5edbf45c0: Confluence of modern soul, jazz, R&B, and Black American guitar tradition · Isaiah Sharkey stands at the confluence of modern soul, jazz, R&B, and Black American guitar tradition, carrying forward a lineage that links George Benson, Curtis Mayfield, Wes Montgomery, and Jimi Hendrix while forging a vocabulary entirely his own. A Grammy Award–winning guitarist, vocalist, composer, and producer, Sharkey has become one of the most respected musicians of his generation—celebrated for his sophisticated harmonic sensibility, unmistakable tone, and ability to shape-shift effortlessly between musical worlds. Born and raised on Chicago’s North Side in a deeply musical family, Sharkey was immersed from childhood in gospel, jazz, and classic R&B. His father, a working musician, recognized early his son’s extraordinary ear and feel, guiding him through professional-level repertoire before most children his age would form basic chords. By the time he was 14, Sharkey was touring nationally; by his late teens, he had already become a first-call session player in Chicago’s tight-knit recording community. Sharkey’s breakthrough into the international spotlight came through his long-standing creative relationship with D’Angelo. His guitar work on D’Angelo’s landmark album Black Messiah earned him a Grammy Award and positioned him among the most innovative guitarists shaping contemporary Black music. From that point forward, Sharkey’s trajectory accelerated: he became a go-to collaborator for a wide range of artists including John Mayer, H.E.R., Robert Glasper, Cory Henry, Lettuce, Chris Dave & The Drumhedz, Lalah Hathaway, Common, Paul Simon, Brian McKnight , Greg Phillinganes, among many others. As a solo artist, Sharkey has developed a distinctive, emotionally resonant sound that blends deep-pocket groove, virtuosic improvisation, and songwriter-driven storytelling. His current album, RED , introduced audiences to his modern fusion of soul, R&B, jazz, and guitar-based narrative. His follow-up projects—each expanding his sonic palette—solidify his standing as an artist capable of speaking fluently to instrumental purists and mainstream audiences alike. Sharkey is equally at home on global festival stages, intimate jazz clubs, and stadium tours. His work has spanned from serving as an MD for Raphael Saadiq's NBA All-Stars televised performance to late-night television appearances to the Grammys televised tribute to Quincy Jones and Blue Note residencies. Yet his most defining characteristic remains his musical integrity: a commitment to depth, craft, and authenticity. A multi-instrumentalist, arranger, and producer, Sharkey’s creative range continues to grow. His forthcoming releases explore new integrations of analog and electronic texture, guitar-forward harmonic architecture, and songwriting rooted in personal truth. Whether performing his own music or elevating the work of others, Sharkey brings the same signature qualities—precision, warmth, spirituality, and an unshakeable sense of groove. Today, Isaiah Sharkey is widely regarded as one of the most vital contemporary voices in the continuum of guitar excellence. His artistry honors his lineage while pushing the idiom forward, ensuring that his influence will resonate for decades to come.

ab61187a-a734-4fe7-b3d9-efcfc0708d78: Embodiment Practices is an invitation to practice giving ourselves permission to arrive fully to where we are, and gently explore movement and stillness to care for our bodies and ourselves. This event happens each week at the Alembic. As an element of self attunement, we will practice making intuitive choices through a lens of self love, meaning that we are each making choices that are nourishing and responsive to ourselves as individuals in that moment. Part of this practice includes being very intentional and explicit about what kinds of choices we might consider, and being curious about how it feels to try them. There will be many options provided throughout, with guidance around how to navigate choice making, including if this is new to you or you are navigating a limitation or injury. There will be a corner of the room set aside in case you’d like to opt out of the facilitated structure and take a moment for yourself to rest. Opening Circle: We'll ground and check-in with whatever feels present for each of us. We get to welcome ourselves to come as we are. Warm Up: We'll do a guided, full-bodied warm up, tuning the instruments of our bodies and attention, giving ourselves time to shake it out, stretch, wiggle, and move through whatever feels stuck. Movements will be simple enough to follow along, giving us a chance to get out of our heads and drop into our bodies, regulating our nervous system. Drawing on contemporary dance and yoga, there will be flow, rhythm, and music. Movement Explorations: We'll explore movements that deepen our connection with our bodies and our intuition, focusing on concepts and areas of the body that can help us settle and release. Meditation: Finally, we'll settle into meditation and rest. Finding stillness might be sitting/standing/lying down and might include cozy props, having eyes open or closed, and suggestions to make yourself comfortable, including allowing some body movement within that quiet space. Please bring clothes you feel comfortable to move in. It’s recommended to bring long sleeves, long pants and socks with you, in case we are moving on the floor. Bring a journal if you’d like. About Suzanne (Zan): With three decades of contemporary/modern dance experience and 15 years of teaching, Suzanne Beahrs guides students in exploring movement as a pathway to deeper connection—with ourselves, our surroundings, and each other. Her classes blend technical training, creative expression, and guidance on being intentional with how we are each practicing. Her movement style was described by The New York Times as “grounded, silken.” In addition to contemporary dance, she is currently heavily influenced by house dance, contact improvisation, and mindfulness practices. She is currently on faculty at Shawl-Anderson Dance Center and teaches around the Bay Area, including ODC, the Berkeley Alembic, and Finnish Hall. Zan has previously taught extensively at Gibney, Elon University, ADF studios, and many more. She has shown her choreography in NY, NC, CA, AZ, MA, and MO, and performed in works by Ishika Seth, Mo Miner, and others. Beyond the studio, Suzanne is a facilitator and has worked as a DEI consultant. She also enjoys exploring writing, visual art, nature, music, and belonging. Education: MFA in Dance, NYU Tisch School of the Arts; BA in Geology, UC Berkeley Learn more about Suzanne, upcoming classes/workshops (contemporary, embodiment, improvisation, contact improvisation and private lessons): IG @suzannebeahrs suzannebeahrs.com

fb1063bb-ea13-4c91-85c0-8f866fbe30f3: Join us for a meet-and-greet signing line personalization opportunity featuring Pete McBride, an award-winning nature photographer, author, explorer, and filmmaker. Pete McBride is an award-winning photographer, filmmaker, writer, and speaker known for his powerful storytelling at the intersection of adventure and environmental conservation. Born and raised in the Rocky Mountains of Colorado, Pete has spent over 25 years capturing the planet’s most awe-inspiring landscapes and natural wonders from Everest and Antarctica to relocating African elephants and swimming with orcas in the Arctic. A National Geographic Explorer, Adventurer of the Year and Sony Artisan of Imagery, McBride has worked in more than 75 countries, combining his skills as a visual storyteller and filmmaker to spotlight pressing environmental issues, particularly those involving water scarcity, public land protection, and climate change. His photography and writing have appeared in National Geographic, Smithsonian, Time, Outside and many others. He is a frequent speaker at corporate conferences, performing arts centers and stages from TEDx and Pixar to the World Economic Forum. His 750-mile trek through the length of the Grand Canyon became the basis for the Emmy-nominated documentary Into the Canyon and his celebrated book The Grand Canyon: Between River and Rim, which won a national outdoor book award. His more recent books, Seeing Silence, and Chasing Water, also won national outdoor book awards, and his latest narrative book, Witness to Water, is a two-decade-long, personal narrative of the Colorado River. Wild Silence, his first children’s book, comes out this November. In 2025, McBride was given The Ansel Adams Award for a lifetime achievement in conservation photography. About the books: Wild Silence: A Photographer's Journeys to the Edges of the Earth In this nonfiction tour around the world for ages 8-12, accompanied by stunning photographs and complementary illustrations, award-winning nature photographer Pete McBride shares his experiences of places in the world where human noise pollution recedes and allows the sounds of the natural world to be heard. The reader accompanies McBride on all seven continents, centered on his tales of memorable encounters with nature and its sounds and anchored with photographs. McBride’s vivid storytelling includes place-based stories, such as the ice on Mount Everest and a close encounter with an avalanche, as well as stories based on encounters with animals like the electric eel he narrowly avoided in the Amazon River. Witness to Water: One Photographer's Mission to Defend the Colorado River Dammed, polluted, and redirected to sustain ever-increasing demand from cities and agriculture, the mighty Colorado River now runs dry more than a hundred miles from where it once met the ocean. Witness to Water chronicles McBride's source-to-sea journey down the Colorado and his mission to fight for conservation and restoration of the river, as well as a similar source-to-sea journey along the Ganges, and the infamous 750- mile hike through the Grand Canyon that would become the subject of New York Times bestseller A Walk in the Park by Kevin Fedarko. The Grand Canyon: Between River and Rim Award-winning photographer Pete McBride takes us on a gripping adventure story through stunning, never-before-seen photography, along with powerful essays from best-selling authors Kevin Fedarko and Hampton Sides. Through his "walk in the park" hiking the entire 750 miles of Grand Canyon National Park—from the Colorado River to the canyon rim—McBride captures the majesty of this natural wonder as he calls on us all to protect America's open-air cathedral. 57aa27b0-ae7b-459b-bf9f-a122d09f1fc6: Join us for a meet-and-greet signing line personalization opportunity featuring Pete McBride, an award-winning nature photographer, author, explorer, and filmmaker. Pete will be in the Bay Area for the MPSF Distinguished Speaker Series from November 30 through December 2. LEARN MORE Pete McBride is an award-winning photographer, filmmaker, writer, and speaker known for his powerful storytelling at the intersection of adventure and environmental conservation. Born and raised in the Rocky Mountains of Colorado, Pete has spent over 25 years capturing the planet’s most awe-inspiring landscapes and natural wonders from Everest and Antarctica to relocating African elephants and swimming with orcas in the Arctic. A National Geographic Explorer, Adventurer of the Year and Sony Artisan of Imagery, McBride has worked in more than 75 countries, combining his skills as a visual storyteller and filmmaker to spotlight pressing environmental issues, particularly those involving water scarcity, public land protection, and climate change. His photography and writing have appeared in National Geographic, Smithsonian, Time, Outside and many others. He is a frequent speaker at corporate conferences, performing arts centers and stages from TEDx and Pixar to the World Economic Forum. His 750-mile trek through the length of the Grand Canyon became the basis for the Emmy-nominated documentary Into the Canyon and his celebrated book The Grand Canyon: Between River and Rim, which won a national outdoor book award. His more recent books, Seeing Silence, and Chasing Water, also won national outdoor book awards, and his latest narrative book, Witness to Water, is a two-decade-long, personal narrative of the Colorado River. Wild Silence, his first children’s book, comes out this November. In 2025, McBride was given The Ansel Adams Award for a lifetime achievement in conservation photography. About the books: Wild Silence: A Photographer's Journeys to the Edges of the Earth In this nonfiction tour around the world for ages 8-12, accompanied by stunning photographs and complementary illustrations, award-winning nature photographer Pete McBride shares his experiences of places in the world where human noise pollution recedes and allows the sounds of the natural world to be heard. The reader accompanies McBride on all seven continents, centered on his tales of memorable encounters with nature and its sounds and anchored with photographs. McBride’s vivid storytelling includes place-based stories, such as the ice on Mount Everest and a close encounter with an avalanche, as well as stories based on encounters with animals like the electric eel he narrowly avoided in the Amazon River. Witness to Water: One Photographer's Mission to Defend the Colorado River Dammed, polluted, and redirected to sustain ever-increasing demand from cities and agriculture, the mighty Colorado River now runs dry more than a hundred miles from where it once met the ocean. Witness to Water chronicles McBride's source-to-sea journey down the Colorado and his mission to fight for conservation and restoration of the river, as well as a similar source-to-sea journey along the Ganges, and the infamous 750- mile hike through the Grand Canyon that would become the subject of New York Times bestseller A Walk in the Park by Kevin Fedarko. The Grand Canyon: Between River and Rim Award-winning photographer Pete McBride takes us on a gripping adventure story through stunning, never-before-seen photography, along with powerful essays from best-selling authors Kevin Fedarko and Hampton Sides. Through his "walk in the park" hiking the entire 750 miles of Grand Canyon National Park—from the Colorado River to the canyon rim—McBride captures the majesty of this natural wonder as he calls on us all to protect America's open-air cathedral. a2d39bbc-448d-49cd-bc2f-eb9818a8623b: Join us for a 30-minute virtual chat with e bond, live over Zoom! e bond is a designer + artist + writer + bookbinder & educator. Currently, she teaches art workshops & creates fabric collections by day, makes handmade books by night, hangs out with trees on weekends and writes something close to poems in the spaces between. Under the studio name roughdrAftbooks, she makes one-of-a-kind artists books, printed pieces and abstract drawings that merge and blur the boundaries of bookbinding, printmaking, surface design and poetry. e’s artist statement reads: What I love to create is consistently interested in investigating relationality. Whether the final forms are words, monotypes, book forms, or any combination, my work maps the connections between disparate thoughts, shapes, and spaces. While questioning each element separately, to uncover new connections, I am discovering not only what is made when two or more entities share a physical space, but also the third space that emerges from this sharing. As someone who loves to work with words and images, my visual interests are closely related to my interests in language structure and meaning. Again, this third space that appears when two words or ideas are placed together. They emerge not only as themselves but as something completely new. e holds a BFA in Graphic Design and Art History from Moore College of Art & Design and an MFA in Creative Writing and Book Art from Mills College. She has spent years as a professor of Graphic Design and Book Art in various college and university art departments, and her work is held in library collections across the US. e’s work has been published in Pressing Matters Magazine, Uppercase Magazine, Berkeley Poetry Review, 500 Handmade Books, as well as numerous books (about books). Most recently, her work has moved into the world of surface design where she designs colorful, abstract fabric collections in collaboration with Free Spirit Fabrics. 1bd7ee3b-954d-407f-9203-a0cbea3b1abd: Melissa Clark is the New York Times bestselling author of Dinner in One , as well as Dinner: Changing the Game , Dinner in an Instant , Comfort in an Instant , Kid in the Kitchen , and Dinner in French . She is a staff writer for The New York Times Food section, where she writes their daily newsletter, and her wildly popular food column, "A Good Appetite." The winner of multiple James Beard and IACP awards, Melissa earned an MFA in writing from Columbia, and her work has been selected for The Best American Food Writing . The Big Book of Dinner- Acclaimed New York Times food writer and James Beard Award–winning author Melissa Clark presents her ultimate guide to cooking just about anything, with 175 any-night recipes—plus 150 tested variations—and lessons to make cooking easy, intuitive, and a total joy. Working with a chef’s creativity for flavor and a home cook’s sensibility for ease, Melissa Clark has been one of America’s favorite recipe creators for decades, helping millions make stunningly great food with flair and no fuss. And now, with The Big Book of Dinner she gives you her ultimate treasure trove: all the recipes you need, the ways to riff off of them, and lessons you learn from them along the way to make you a great cook. She shares the building blocks that make these recipes work, so you’ll know exactly how to follow them to perfection, or how to go off-script if you want and to make it your own. With Melissa’s friendly instructions guiding the way, you can take classic Italian-American Meatballs , and switch them up with aromatic spices reminiscent of Middle Eastern kibbe, or use them in an easy sheet-pan dinner with roasted vegetables. Super-quick Sweet and Spicy Chicken with Cumin and Honey can be transformed with ginger and marmalade for a fresh punch, or honey mustard and lemon for a different spin. Throughout, there are signature Melissa favorites like Creamy Corn Pasta with Tomatoes and Chile Flakes , lessons on cooking the perfect steak or nailing a braise every time, plenty of vegetables and plant-based dishes, a baker’s dozen (and then some) of perfect desserts, and beautiful photographs for every recipe. Whether you’re a novice in the kitchen or a longtime cook, a devotee of Melissa’s or just getting to know her, The Big Book of Dinner will be your cooking companion for a lifetime.

71a7812d-52d3-4895-9876-df80fa400fe6: The hidden history of American radicals abroad · One night in 1940, a group of Stalinists opened fire on Leon Trotsky’s compound in Mexico City. By the time the shooting was over, Trotsky lived to die another day—but his bodyguard, a young American named Sheldon Harte, had been killed. For investigative journalist Julia Harte, the quest to uncover the truth about Sheldon—her father’s second cousin—was just the beginning of her discovery. Her new book, Americans Without Borders: The Radical Activists Who Fought for US Ideals Abroad While Facing Political Persecution at Home reveals the hidden two-hundred-year history of Americans who traveled abroad to join revolutionary liberation movements—and in return were labeled radicals by the U.S. government. The remarkable stories Harte uncovers include those of Black veterans of the Spanish Civil War who helped launch the civil rights movement; the forgotten Native American contingent in Nicaragua’s Sandinista/Contra conflict; Elaine Mokhtefi’s work with the Algerian National Liberation Front; and Melinda Paras and her organization of Filipinos against the repressive US-backed Marcos regime. Through meticulous research and on-the-ground reporting, Harte brings her subjects to life in deeply personal detail, exploring not only their heroic sides but also the tensions between their actions and ideals. Interrogating how and why activists were branded as threats by an expanding security state, Americans Without Borders asks what makes a ‘radical’. Join author Julia Harte for a conversation about the long history of transnational radicalism as an irrepressibly American tradition. She’ll be joined by journalist, writer, and producer Sonia Paul . Julia Harte is an investigative reporter in New York City. For the past decade, she has covered U.S. national affairs and the Justice Department for Reuters. Her writing has also appeared in publications including Harper's Magazine , The Nation , Slate , National Geographic , The Center for Public Integrity , and Lapham's Quarterly . Sonia Paul is an award-winning independent journalist, writer, and producer who specializes in investigating how power hierarchies and transnational issues impact state systems and individual and community identities. Her stories have been published widely, in outlets like WIRED , Mother Jones , Harper’s Magazine , NPR, 99% Invisible and BBC World Service. She is also the host of a new podcast from Berkeley Social Sciences and a forthcoming podcast based on her reporting.

9d395710-43c2-4beb-81e2-2c09a78c0914: Bookshop West Portal cannot wait to host renowned science fiction author of the Mars trilogy, The Ministry for the Future , and The High Sierra: A Love Story, and lifelong advocate for the wilderness and the environment, Kim Stanley Robinson. Join us to celebrate his new book, The Best Journey in the World: An Antarctic Story , a gripping story of adventure that brilliantly intertwines memoir and polar history. Learn about one of the most perilous places on our planet, how it shaped out history, and it’s importance for our future. You won't want to miss the truly stunning never-before-seen photography either! This event is FREE to attend. Seating is first-come, first-served. (RSVPs are optional, but encouraged for our planning purposes.) About the Book: Interweaving memoir, some never-before-published photographs, and good old fashioned ice adventure, Kim Stanley Robinson takes readers along on the Arctic journeys that have happened before and the journeys that may never happen again. In May of 1911, Robert Scott and the twenty-four men under his command said good-bye to the sun and settled in for the long Antarctic winter. When the sun returned in September, they were going to try to become the first people to reach the South Pole. However, a week past the winter solstice, Scott's second-in-command took a team on a trip to Cape Crozier to man-haul two sledges through the perpetual night of the Antarctic winter, exposed to the coldest temperatures human beings had ever traveled in. This side trip was, at best, a dangerous distraction and at worst, a disaster. Yet, chronicled by zoological assistant (and major expedition funder) Apsley Cherry-Garrard, it became The Worst Journey in the World , one of the best adventure books ever written. Kim Stanley Robinson first read Cherry-Garrard's book in his twenties and re-read it again in 1995, as part of his preparations to Antarctica that he made that year as research for his Mars novels. It was a dream excursion: he traveled around the continent, by snowmobile and helicopter and airplane. All the while, Cherry's book loomed larger and larger in Robinson's mind, and he tried to follow in their ill-fated footsteps. Ultimately, in The Best Journey in the World , we see Robinson stepping on ice and finding an earthly holy place. As he searches for what can--and cannot--be found again, he takes readers on a journey of realization that is not just about being the first to get somewhere but about falling in love with what the world has to offer us. That being with people who also feel a kinship to a place worthy of preserving is itself, an act of devotion. Replete with gorgeous photographs taken in a place many will never set foot, and woven throughout with Robinson's sharp, funny, and personal voice, prepare to take the best journey in the world. One of the New Yorker's Most Anticipated Fall Reads About the Author: Kim Stanley Robinson is the author of more than twenty books, including the bestselling Mars trilogy, The Ministry for the Future , and The High Sierra: A Love Story . He was a featured speaker at COP26 in Glasgow, at the UN’s Summit of the Future in 2024, and at COP30 in Belém, Brazil. His work has been translated into thirty languages, and in 2016 asteroid 72432 was named Kimrobinson. He lives in Davis, California.

A Night of Gospel Brilliance, Soul & Praise · Join us for an unforgettable night of Gospel, Soul, and Praise as we usher in the holiday season with the angelic voice of gospel singer-songwriter Sylvia Anderson and her anointed guest, Grammy Award winner Darrel Walls, gospel legend Derrick Hall, and the music direction and ministry of Carl Wheeler. Presented by Sylvia Anderson & Mark Elliott of the A-list Musiq Circle - Your Bay Area Who's Who Entertainment network. With Special Guest Host TBA. A gifted gospel artist with an angelic voice and a heart devoted to ministry, Sylvia Anderson has spent over 40 years using her God-given talent to inspire, uplift, and spread the love of Jesus Christ. Born into a family rich in musical and spiritual heritage, her journey began at the tender age of five when she discovered her ability to sing. Guided by her father, a preacher and singer, and her mother, a vocalist, she was nurtured in a household where music and faith were inseparable. She first sang with the Coleman Sisters, under the influence of her father, Willie Coleman, and continued to grow musically, sharing her voice with groups such as Derrick Hall & Company and the Center of Hope Choir. Her remarkable gift has also led her to sing background for gospel greats, including Tramaine Hawkins and Nona Brown, and appear on BET’s renowned Bobby Jones Gospel Hour. A true musician, she’s sung in concerts, gospel festivals, weddings, homegoing services and private events, further enhancing her ability to minister through music. In addition to her musical journey, she has served faithfully in ministry and is currently a minister at Covenant Worship Center in Berkeley, California. Beyond the stage, she is deeply committed to serving her community. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Theology and is the owner of a care home for children, as well as actively involved in foster care initiatives—demonstrating her passion for nurturing and uplifting the next generation. A woman of many roles, she is a devoted mother of three, a loving wife, grandmother, sister, and friend. For over 30 years, she has also worked as a professional hairstylist, touching lives both inside and outside the church, and retired after 33 years from the medical field. Rooted in Oakland, California, her life’s mission is simple yet powerful: to send God’s love through every song, every act of service, and every life she encounters. Her favorite song, “Because He Lives,” reflects the foundation of her faith and the message she carries wherever she goes. Darrel Walls is the eldest sibling and eldest member of The Walls Group, the acclaimed four-sibling group celebrated for their distinctive harmonies, musicianship, and progressive sound. A gifted vocalist, musician, and creative force, Darrel has long been an integral part of the group’s unmistakable musical identity. Stepping into his own as a solo artist, he recorded his debut solo project, Heart of Mine, with Grammy-winning artist and producer PJ Morton, earning the 2026 Grammy Award for Best Gospel Album. His breakout solo season has continued with three Stellar Award wins, including Artist of the Year and Contemporary Male Artist of the Year, while his single “ABLE” reached No. 1 on Billboard’s Gospel Airplay chart. His solo journey has further established him as one of gospel music’s standout voices. While continuing to bring his unmistakable sound to The Walls Group, Darrel is building an exciting solo legacy of his own.

Hiromi will be in Japan February 1-21 but will resume classes when she gets back Hiromi Vardy is a certified Zen Shiatsu, Yang style Tai Chi, and Zhineng Qigong healer and practitioner. She first encountered Tai Chi in 1973 while studying theater design and performance art in London. Initially drawn to the beauty of the movements, she soon discovered that the practice had a profound effect on her consciousness, awakening a deep interest in the healing arts. While collaborating on stage with dancers in London, Hiromi began treating injuries in overworked bodies. In 1976, after a serious accident that resulted in loss of circulation in her leg and concern about possible amputation, she turned to daily Tai Chi practice, self-massage, and treatment from a Japanese acupuncturist. This experience became a turning point in her healing journey and led her back to Japan, where she studied Shiatsu at the Namikoshi School and trained at the Zen Shiatsu Center under Shizuto Masunaga. After moving to the United States with her family in 1987, Hiromi continued deepening her practice and teaching. During a period of significant stress later in her life, she encountered Master Ming Tong Gu and began studying Zhineng (wisdom healing) Qigong under his guidance, eventually becoming licensed to teach. The healing shift she experienced through this practice was profound and continues to inform her teaching today. Since 2013, Hiromi has been dedicated to teaching Zhineng Qigong, expanding her offerings to include online classes in 2020. Her work invites students to explore the foundations of Qigong and Tai Chi as embodied, healing practices that cultivate awareness, vitality, and resilience.

Founded on Grand Avenue in 2006 and relocating to 25th Street in 2009, the gallery has sustained a thriving artist-run business with a commitment to artistic independence. Mercury Twenty has built an extensive network of artists—21 current members and more than 60 alumni—who together have shaped Oakland’s creative landscape. Gallery members played a role in the early development of Oakland Art Murmur and helped establish the 25th Street arts district. Through two decades of artistic exploration and collaboration, Mercury Twenty is a vibrant and enduring presence in Oakland’s cultural life. For this milestone exhibition, current members and participating alumni have been organized into small curatorial teams. Thoughtfully assembled, these groups bring together different artistic perspectives and practices, creating unexpected visual connections and engaging conversations between works. Curated by gallery member Jill McLennan, the exhibition features a dynamic range of paintings, photography, sculpture, printmaking, quilts, mixed media, and installations that reflect the diversity and creative energy that has defined Mercury Twenty throughout its history. About the Book Everyone's favorite TV and podcast host is back ... with a vengeance. After realizing that every win in her life came right after being underestimated, rejected, or told she wasn't enough, Keltie Knight decided to build a theory around it: The F*ck Them Theory. Part memoir, part manifesto, The F*ck Them Theory is your permission slip to stop apologizing and start transforming rejection into power. It's not about bitterness, it's about alchemy. It's about turning humiliation into humor, heartbreak into healing, and rage into reinvention. Keltie goes where most "empowerment" books don't dare. She shares raw, unfiltered stories from behind the curtain--the breakdowns, the pills, the plastic surgery, the feud the tabloids never caught, and the family secrets she's never shared ... until now. The F*ck Them Theory is for anyone who's been underestimated or is tired of being "grateful for the opportunity" when they deserved so much more. If you've ever wanted a best friend who tells the truth, drops the act, and still shows up in sequins, then welcome home. About the Author Keltie Knight is a three-time Emmy Award–winning television personality, New York Times bestselling author, and People’s Choice Award–nominated podcast host. She currently hosts E! Live From The Red Carpet and is widely known for her work on Entertainment Tonight, The Insider, and CBS’s SUPERFAN, which she also created and executive produced. As co-creator and host of the hit podcast LadyGang, with over 300 million downloads and a New York Times bestselling book, Knight has built a pop-culture empire rooted in female friendship, ambition, and unapologetic authenticity. Her fashion and cultural influence have been featured in Vogue, Elle, and The New York Times. Keltie spearheaded and created LADYWORLD, the first-ever podcast festival dedicated to female voices, bringing together over 3,000 attendees and generating more than $1M in brand partnerships. Positioned at the forefront of innovation in the female podcast space, she continues to develop new formats that expand how audiences experience content, community, and live events. A sought-after content creator and brand ambassador, Keltie has developed long-term partnerships with brands such as Marshalls and Fabletics, consistently translating audience trust into high-performing, multi-platform campaigns. Her first full length solo book "The F*CK Them Theory: Self-Help For People Who are Done Being the Bigger Person was released through Blackstone Publishing Nov. 2026. In addition to her on-air work, Knight is an investor and advisor to ALTA, an AI-powered fashion technology platform recently named to Time’s 100 Best Inventions of the Year, recognized by Vogue as a Best Invention, and announced as an official AI fashion partner of the Council of Fashion Designers of America (CFDA). About Yemanjo Yemanjo is the musical project of Bay Area producer, DJ, singer, and multi-instrumentalist Ben Harris. His collaborations span the globe, including musicians from Mali, Colombia, Morocco, Kenya, Brazil, and Egypt, and he has worked with artists such as Novalima, El Búho, and Chancha Via Circuito. His 2026 album Semillas de Poder ("Seeds of Power"), created with Venezuelan singer Irene Rosalia, is a lush exploration of Latin folktronica, nature, and the reclamation of spiritual power through our connection to the living world. About Matt Barkin Matt Barkin is a breathwork and meditation practitioner with over 15 years of experience exploring the transformative potential of contemplative practice. Rooted in the traditions of Vipassana meditation, Kriya Yoga, and the ancient yogic art of pranayama, his approach to breathwork invites participants to access expanded states of awareness and reconnect with their innate capacity for healing. He is also a writer and filmmaker.

DEMOLA the VIOLINIST BIO: Demola, known to fans as “Demola the Violinist,” is an internationally recognized musician, songwriter, multi-instrumentalist, record producer, and award-winning self-taught multi-genre violinist. Born in Lagos, Nigeria, Demola moved to the United States to pursue his solo music career, blending his love for Afrobeat, reggae, R&B, hip-hop, pop, and country into a sound that is distinctly his own. In 2024, Demola’s career reached new heights, fueled by his vibrant social media presence and viral performances. With over 6 million followers and millions of streams across Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, his videos regularly attract millions of views, making him one of the most-followed and celebrated violinists worldwide. His performances captivate global audiences, and his fanbase continues to expand with each viral hit. This year, Demola launched his highly successful “One in a Million 2.0” tour, performing in over 20 cities and mesmerizing audiences with original songs like “ONE IN A MILLION,” “MBAPPE,” and “LOVA,” which have collectively amassed millions of streams. He also made waves with his feature on the song “FORGIVE OUR TRESPASSES,” showcasing viral Afrobeat across the US and performing at Coachella. A hometown hero in Houston, Texas, Demola, has performed the national anthem for major sports teams, including the Houston Astros, Rockets, Dynamo, and Texans, before crowds of up to 70,000 people. He has also shared the stage with country music star Jelly Roll, performing for 74,000 fans at the Houston Rodeo. Demola is a fan favorite on television as well, with appearances on Good Morning America Online, FOX 26 Houston, CultureMap Houston, 97.9 KBXX Houston, FOX 31 Denver, WGN-9 Chicago, Black News Channel, and many others. His innovative fusion of genres has made him one of the first artists of his kind, captivating listeners with the melodic beauty of his violin and proving that he is truly one in a million. 99913346-aaf5-45fa-abc6-dd2567b0fec2: With its humor, candor, delightful illustrations, and (of course) a bit of implied profanity, Get Off That Screen! is a gift book for adults that will resonate with ANYONE trying to raise, educate, or connect with kids in this digital age: from parents, caregivers, and grandparents to teachers, coaches, and therapists—and every adult in between. Willow will be joined in conversation by San Francisco author Erin Gordon. More than just “a balm for our shared exasperation”, Get Off That Screen! includes an Afterword with practical guidelines from author and parenting/technology expert Katherine Martinko and an extensive Resources section with books, events, and organizations to help families enjoy screen-free time, together. Is your kid’s obsession with screens driving you nuts? Do you spend your days begging and bribing your kiddo to “ Get off that screen! ”? This book can’t eliminate screen addiction (including, ahem , your own). But it can help you vent your frustrations about raising kids in the digital age. Willow Older’s lighthearted approach to a serious problem will make you giggle and groan—and you’ll find tips for reducing your family’s screen time, too. “An all-too-relatable tribute to the challenge of prying kids—and ourselves!—off of screens.” —Catherine Price, #1 New York Times bestselling author of How to Break Up With Your Phone “Willow Older injects some much-needed humor and hope into an otherwise overwhelming topic.”— Katherine Martinko, author of Hold the Phone and Childhood Unplugged and creator of The Analog Family newsletter “Just what the doctor ordered for the screen-addicted generation.”— Zibby Owens, host of the “Totally Booked” podcast “This whimsical tale is a balm for our shared exasperation.”— Tiffany Shlain, artist, Emmy-nominated filmmaker, and author of 2 4/6: Giving up Screens One Day a Week to Get More Time, Creativity, and Connection “A Shel Silverstein-esque author for the digital age, Willow Older makes you laugh out loud and feel seen in the best of ways.”— Erin Gordon, author of PEEPS and Look What You Made Me Do Willow Older is an author, illustrator, speaker, and ghostwriter in Mill Valley. She’s the co-founder of Today I Noticed mindfulness and the co-author of Today I Noticed: A Little Book of Mindfulness that Will Change the Way You See the World (Blue Star Press, 2023). For that book, which is now in its third printing and has been translated into multiple languages, Willow and her co-author, Deborah Huber, were thrilled to hold their launch event in front of a large and enthusiastic crowd at Book Passage, where all 40+ books in stock sold out. Erin Gordon is a San Francisco author whose work spans fiction, memoir and contemporary romance. A Stanford-trained journalist, she brings decades of reporting and storytelling experience to her conversation with Willow Older. a7eda846-bcf2-4e20-977a-eded1b1a9e6c: Special Guest Gallery Chat: Questions 27 & 28 with Author Karen Tei Yamashita from Join acclaimed author Karen Tei Yamashita for a Special Guest Gallery Chat in conjunction with OMCA’s current exhibition, Be Here / 1942: A New Lens on the Japanese American Incarceration . Born in Oakland in 1951, Yamashita is a member of the Sansei generation, the grandchildren of Japanese immigrants. With both of her parents incarcerated at Topaz, Utah, during World War II, Yamashita brings a personal connection to this history. Centering her novel Questions 27 & 28 , she will invite visitors to consider the questions and their enduring significance in relation to Japanese American incarceration, identity, memory, and belonging. Copies of the novel will be available in the OMCA Shop for purchase. Get Museum Admission Tickets Member Tickets About Karen Tei Yamashita: Karen Tei Yamashita is the author of ten books, including I Hotel , finalist for the National Book Award. In 2024 Yamashita was inducted as a Literature Fellow in the American Academy of Arts and Sciences. cf259e5b-4a75-49a1-8df7-df1aedef022b: This richly illustrated lecture* will take us into a world of ocean navigation largely unknown to the West, a world in which the traditional navigator’s only directional tools are the stars, the ocean swells and the flight paths of birds. In 1983 and 1984 I spent eleven months on Satawal Island and in the Western Carolines as an apprentice to Mau Piailug, then one of the last paliuw, captains fully initiated in the Talk of Navigation, the closely guarded, ancient practices around reading the cosmos and the seas. I chronicled my experiences and the navigational techniques in the book The Last Navigator, first published in 1987, and a documentary film of the same title for PBS in 1988. Now some forty years on I have updated the stories with a new generation of Satawalese islanders and researchers in the revised and fully illustrated edition of The Last Navigator. *Original photographs and film footage, 1983-1987 The classic account of traditional Micronesian navigation and “the last navigator,” Mau Piailug, who fought to preserve it—now available in a revised edition illustrated in full color As a young man piloting a small sailboat across the Pacific, Steve Thomas developed a fascination with ancient methods of navigation. He learned that, for thousands of years, the peoples of Oceania had sailed unerringly across the Pacific without compass or charts, guided only by natural signs—stars, waves, and the flight paths of birds. In search of this secret knowledge, Thomas traveled to the tiny island of Satawal in Micronesia, home to Mau Piailug, one of the few surviving paliuw , or navigators. In The Last Navigator , Thomas tells how he convinced Piailug to accept him as his student and teach him the closely guarded Talk of Navigation. It is a remarkable book, offering at once a clear and precise account of Micronesian wayfinding and the moving story of one man trying to preserve his culture against the tide of modernity. Now, forty years after his original journey to study under Mau Piailug, Thomas has worked with a new generation of researchers, including natives of Satawal, to prepare this revised edition of The Last Navigator . All Satawalese words are rendered in the now-accepted orthography, and the islanders, originally identified by pseudonyms, appear under their true names. And throughout, Thomas has added a generous selection of color photographs from his time on Satawal, documenting the island, its people, and its seafaring culture. This result is a lasting tribute to the spirit of the Satawalese, and to the Talk of Navigation A fascinating exploration of a remoted archipelago and its seagoing people — Peter Matthiessen If you have any interest in the sea and navigation or in the impact of colonialism on indigenous cultures, or if you just enjoy a well-told story of adventure, then read on. — from the foreword by David Barrie [Thomas] is a dual explorer, simultaneously trying to rediscover an ancient system of sailing, using only nature’s navigational signals, and trying to find himself in the myth-made culture of Micronesia. . . . [This] is a travel book with a dream. — Los Angeles Times Book Review This is a story of adventure, and coming of age. It is also an important document, preserving an ancient oral tradition. — San Francisco Chronicle Steve Thomas is familiar to television viewers as the two-time Emmy award-winning host of This Old House, Renovation Nation, and Save Our History. But he is also an experienced home builder and sailor. Beginning in 1977, he sailed a 43-foot wooden sloop from England to San Francisco via the Panama Canal, Galapagos, Marquesas, and Hawaii. In the early 1980’s, he journeyed to the remote Micronesian island of Satawal to learn the ancient technique of star path navigation, an experience that resulted in this book as well as a documentary for the PBS series Adventure. A throwback to family reads of yore, this epic follows a troubled boy and a host of hilariously vexed animals who must save a river before it’s dammed, so they can save themselves. Gabriel (“G” for short) is wasting away in the Abiddon County Juvenile Center when he’s introduced to the Shongunk River by his dying uncle. The river valley—trash-heaped but chock-full of mysteries and fish—wins G over. But, as G has learned, good things can’t last. The Shongunk is scheduled to be dammed by a local developer. In a matter of days, it will cease flowing, and all of the talkative creatures who live there in the river valley will be as homeless as G. Just as G decides it’s no time to accept his fate, so too do the animals. To inspire an uprising, a young trout is nominated to make a fateful journey up the river; a raccoon swears a violent oath against humans; and a newly sober buck leads his skittish flock out of harm’s way. Together with G, they show that good can triumph and that there is power in all of us, even the smallest minnow. KIRK LOMBARD is an author, angler, sustainable fishmonger, and tuba player who once worked inside the juvenile rehabilitation system. His first book, the award-winning Sea Forager’s Guide to the Northern California Coast , was described as “poetry” for fish by NPR. He lives in Half Moon Bay with his family, raising his children on herring and sea shanties.

7568d7b0-1f3e-47d0-acf1-58a1de7fa74b: Throwin’ Bo’s presents: Dagmar Zuniga Nicaraguan-American artist Dagmar Zuniga makes music that feels both intimate and expansive: songs drift like disrupted signals, carried by harmony, tape hiss, and a strong sense of touch. Her debut solo album in filth your mystery is kingdom / far smile peasant in yellow music — written and recorded in New York, Norway, and Athens, Georgia over a period of five years on her longtime companion, the Tascam 424 — was released by the People’s Coalition of Tandy on Bandcamp & YouTube in January 2025, accompanied by a small tape run that sold out instantly. The project quickly garnered over two hundred thousand views and the attention of artists such as Mount Eerie, who invited her to tour with them that summer. This year, what was once a jewel of tapped-in algorithms and message boards will meet the world at large, with in filth arriving digitally on March 4 , and physically on April 10 , via AD 93 . in filth is an atmospheric, devotional collage where one voice multiplies into a chorus of selves, sometimes delicate, sometimes severe; an effect created by Zuniga’s masterful layering of texture and complex harmonies. Synths glitter out like spears of sunlight from beneath clouds of moody, time-distorted guitars, and songs spin about themselves like tightly-wound music boxes, making use of a kind of hypnotic repetition, before melting apart into their components or slipping into the following track. Zuniga began recording to tape as a teenager, drawn to the physicality of the medium — how a tape recording is fragile, mutable, and alive. Though her ethereal sound may draw easy comparisons to other female pioneers of psychedelic folk, she is influenced just as much by the darker sounds of Syd Barrett and The Fall. Like Barrett, Zuniga is a painter, and she is interested not only in recording music but in creating a full, self-contained artistic universe: she creates her own artwork, merchandise, music videos, and bootleg tapes of new and unfinished music that she exclusively sells at live shows ( “If something is not material, it does not exist,” she insists). Her world has not gone unvisited, garnering her a monthly show on NTS Radio ‘World of Pain’, as well as a forthcoming appearance at Rewire Festival in April 2026. Though Zuniga’s work explores themes of solitude and suffering, the suffering in her songs is not borrowed or displayed; it is held, then opened outward through empathy — an exacting practice of attention that insists on shared ground. Solitude, in her work, is not withdrawal but a starting point for connection. Likewise, over time, her recording process has become increasingly communal, with in filth featuring musicians across the globe. Newer recordings widen the circle even more. For Zuniga, collaboration is a way to “find a place between worlds,” echoing Badiou’s idea of love as a vision refracted through the prism of difference. Meaning emerges there — in the space between voices, between artist and listener. “I hope my music helps people work through difficult experiences,” she says. “The same way it helps me.” Bandcamp | IG Support to be announced DOORS at 7:00PM | MUSIC at 8:00 PM Tickets

Please come prepared to discuss the book and its themes. We will be focusing on the book, not the TV series based on the book. **We will meet at Firehouse Coffee, but if many people are expected to join the location may change to accommodate our group. The Handmaid's Tale Synopsis (from GoodReads) - The Handmaid’s Tale is a novel of such power that the reader will be unable to forget its images and its forecast. Set in the near future, it describes life in what was once the United States and is now called the Republic of Gilead, a monotheocracy that has reacted to social unrest and a sharply declining birthrate by reverting to, and going beyond, the repressive intolerance of the original Puritans. The regime takes the Book of Genesis absolutely at its word, with bizarre consequences for the women and men in its population. The story is told through the eyes of Offred, one of the unfortunate Handmaids under the new social order. In condensed but eloquent prose, by turns cool-eyed, tender, despairing, passionate, and wry, she reveals to us the dark corners behind the establishment’s calm facade, as certain tendencies now in existence are carried to their logical conclusions. The Handmaid’s Tale is funny, unexpected, horrifying, and altogether convincing. It is at once scathing satire, dire warning, and a tour de force. It is Margaret Atwood at her best.

Skan dares to descend into the hidden chambers of our emotional life - the places shaped by fear, anger, and old wounds. In this gentle yet fearless unraveling, our inner landscape begins to breathe again. And in that renewed freedom, the heart remembers its own language - longing, love, and the ecstatic expression of joy. We'll explore: • Habitual patterns of armoring (holding) and breath-holds • Breath, movement, and sound/voice as pathways to feeling • Relational presence and attunement with clear choice and consent You may leave with: • Fuller breathing and more bodily ease • Emotional release and renewed vitality • Simple practices for listening to your body's signals. You can slow down, opt out, or simply observe at any time. Please purchase your ticket in advance, as we cannot guarantee entry for walk-ins. We recommend arriving 15 minutes early to allow time for check-in and settling in. TEACHER BIO: Lydia Becker is a highly experienced Skan practitioner and instructor, with over 40 years of dedication to the healing arts. 9ae38d6e-2189-4135-9c90-4d42a85e9ae5: A joyful, mischievous, heartfelt book for children and the grown-ups who love them. Recommended for ages 6–10, parents, grandparents, teachers, and anyone who wants to remember what it feels like to live with curiosity, courage, humor, and heart. The Braunicles invite readers into the wonderfully imperfect world of a spirited little boy named Braun. A world filled with adventure, mischief, big feelings, unexpected lessons, and an irresistible enthusiasm for life. Written by Jennifer Levi, the stories are warm, funny, honest, and deeply human. Jennifer gives a distinctive voice and captures childhood in a way that feels both whimsical and completely real: the bold ideas, the questionable decisions, the enormous emotions, the funny family dynamics, and the little moments that often become the memories we treasure most. At its heart, The Braunicles is about living fully. Braun approaches the world with curiosity. He takes chances. He includes people. He makes mistakes. He loves fiercely. He finds fun where others might not see it. And through each story, young readers discover that some of the qualities that make a child challenging, surprising, loud, adventurous, or different can also become their greatest strengths. For parents and grandparents, there is another layer. These stories are a gentle reminder not to rush through childhood trying to make everything perfect. Sometimes the mess is the memory. Sometimes the mischievous child becomes the unforgettable adult. Sometimes the moments that make us shake our heads today are exactly the stories we will tell for the rest of our lives. Jennifer’s voice brings humor and perspective to parenting without preaching. That makes The Braunicles more than a children’s book. -It is a book children can enjoy for adventure. -It is a book parents can recognize themselves in. -It is a book grandparents can give with meaning. -And it is a book families can read together and talk about long after the final page. Jennifer Levi is the founder of The Live Like Braun Foundation and the force behind The Live Like Braun movement. Since the death of her son in May 2025, Jennifer has become a powerful advocate for DUI awareness and meaningful legislative change, passing a new Bill in CA, testifying at the CA State Capitol and on Capitol Hill. She regularly speaks to audiences at DUI workshops and schools all over Southern CA. She serves on MADD's CA State Legislative Board. Jennifer’s advocacy has been featured across multiple media outlets and television networks including NBC, ABC, Fox, and CBS, along with well-known podcasts hosted by Dr. Phil, Kennedy, Jason Kennedy, Amanda Kloots, Kelly Gores, Meghan Judge, and Kate Casey. Jennifer has spoken openly about the profound transformation of her life following the death of her son. She has become a featured contributor to Maria Shriver’s Sunday Paper, writing about the ways grief has reshaped her life with raw honesty, deep emotion, and a touch of irreverence. She hopes The Braunicles inspires children to embrace exactly who they are and encourages grown-ups to give young people the freedom to let their brightest, silliest, most authentic selves shine. Jennifer is a mother, wife, advocate, writer, and former TV executive. Although she has worn many hats, she has always said she is most proud of her role as mom to her two children, Adelle and Braun. She lives in Pacific Palisades, California, with her family and two very naughty dogs. That can feel painful or lonely when we’ve had meaningful journeys (and also when we’ve had disappointing journeys!). Healing – especially from interpersonal injuries – deepens when done in community. The same is true of personal and spiritual growth. Even the most joyful experiences are best metabolized when witnessed. Together, we become a mosaic – a colorful and varied community, greater together than the sum of our parts. Mosaic is a psychedelic integration circle for self-identified women. Here, you’ll find a supportive space to integrate the lessons, challenges, and wisdom from psychedelic journeys so that you can apply those learnings to everyday life. Together, we’ll seek to understand our psychedelic experiences and make profound insights accessible and actionable. This is a drop-in, monthly supported peer group rather than a psychotherapy group. We create space for sharing stories and experiences, receiving support, and forging genuine connections. Whether you’re new to integration or looking to deepen your practice, you’ll find a supportive community here. Dr. Lyssa Menard is a psychologist, psychedelic therapist, and professor (Northwestern University Medical School) with specialties in Integrative Medicine, trauma treatment, and health psychology. 2c5ebbc8-b832-44d7-b506-ed7d6bfef162: (Please do not bring infants to the show) A hippie, activist, lesbian, feminist, lawyer, judge’s search for identity & justice. The at times humorous and at times deadly serious show begins when Amy moves to Berkeley in the early 1970’s during second wave feminism. Amy finds her identity as a lesbian feminist, goes to law school to fight for women’s rights, represents coal miners and battered women in Appalachia and returns to California to open a lesbian feminist law practice. She is representing women who had been sexually harassed – pre-Anita Hill – but keeps seeing all sides of things, becomes an administrative judge and starts a law firm to do mediation and impartial investigations of harassment and discrimination. She adopts two children – both biracial – and experiences racism up close and personal. In the meantime, she can’t stop revisiting her first experience with the criminal justice system in 1970 when she accompanied a friend to a rape trial. Her (white) friend had been raped by a (Black) boyfriend. The friend wanted him to get help, rather than serve a decade in prison. This restorative justice solution was not an option. Amy wonders about her role in the verdict and if real justice is possible in an unjust world. Content Advisories: The content of this production includes topics and events that may be triggering to some people including sexual violence/rape, sexual harassment, racism and familial violence.
2e492e1d-b937-4bfa-8dc3-c3bbf2700288: Poetry, Translation and the Passage of Time · As a young poet in Taiwan in the 1960’s, Fang Xin (方 莘) heard Rachmaninoff’s Second Piano Concerto by chance on the radio. The music left him with a feeling he carried into a poem, 夜的變奏 Night falls so impatiently . The poem was soon incorporated into his first poetry collection, published in Taiwan in Chinese. Six decades later, in the 2020’s, he returned to that poem in English from his home in Oakland, California. What began as an encounter between music and poetry became an encounter between languages, cultures, and two moments in a single life. Join us at Clio's for a conversation with bilingual poet and translator Fang Xin , celebrating the publication of Mo Bai 60 (In Prostration 60) 膜拜 60 , a bilingual reimagining of his first poetry collection, originally published in Taiwan in 1963. In conversation with Fang will be David Roderick , poet, editor, and director of Berkeley's Left Margin LIT. Continuing a conversation they began in The Georgia Review , the two poets will explore how music shapes a writer's ear, what is lost and discovered in translation, and what a lifetime of listening makes possible on the page. The evening begins with a short introduction from cultural anthropologist, writer, and Clio's founding member Cari Borja , reflecting on translation as an act of creation, and how ideas, sensations, and memories travel across artistic forms, languages, geographies, and generations. Fang Xin 方莘 is a bilingual poet and translator. Born in Chengdu in 1939, he moved with his family to Taipei in 1949 and joined the Blue Star Poetry Society as a teenager. His debut collection, 膜拜 Mo bai (In Prostration) , appeared in 1963 and earned acclaim in Taiwan. He has lived in the San Francisco Bay Area since 1982. Mo Bai 60 (In Prostration 60) 膜拜 60, Fang’s second book, published in 2026, is a volume consisting of two books in Chinese and English: Mo bai in its original Chinese text, incorporating recent works, and works in the author’s own translation. David Roderick is the author of Darkness for Beginners , forthcoming in 2027 from Omnidawn. His other books include The Americans , winner of the Julie Suk Award, and Blue Colonial , winner of the APR /Honickman Prize. Additional honors include a Wallace Stegner Fellowship from Stanford University, the Amy Lowell Traveling Scholarship, and a National Endowment for the Arts Fellowship. Roderick edits for The Adroit Journal and serves as the director of Left Margin LIT, a creative writing center and workspace in Berkeley.

03bdf6b3-02c1-4442-8903-ab312ec711e4: Sunday Reset Yoga: Yin & Restorative Say goodbye to the Sunday scaries. Sunday Reset Yoga is your antidote. It’s a gentle, grounding class that blends yin and restorative yoga to help you slow down, let go and start your week from a place of calm. In yin, we use props to support us in longer, quiet poses that go deeper than the muscles and help release tension in the connective tissues and ligaments. In restorative yoga, we’re fully supported by bolsters and blocks, so the body can let go and the mind can follow in a calm cascade of surrender motions. The nervous system can safely shift into the rest and digest mode. There’s no flow to keep up with and nothing to perfect. 9ce758cf-5dc4-408b-a89d-dc13e5067980: Making sense of a holiday tradition. · When it first premiered in St. Petersburg in 1892, the Nutcracker was a colossal flop. It’s easy to see why. Loosely based on an 1816 novella in which an old man gives his goddaughter a doll that comes to life and wages war, the ballet limps through an uneven narrative sprinkled with vague stakes, milquetoast heroes, and culturally insensitive motifs. And yet The Nutcracker is now an unshakeable holiday tradition. The ballet (first performed in the United States by San Francisco Ballet in 1944) marks a rite of passage for dancers, a financial lifeline for dance companies, and an annual tradition for audiences. Versions vary from waltzing flowers to Sugar Plums who tap, skate, stomp, shimmy, and even pop & lock. Its musical score is ubiquitous during the holidays. How did this happen? Janine Kovac , former professional ballet dancer and author of The Nutcracker Chronicles: A Fairytale Memoir, sits down with Shanthi Sekaran ( Lucky Boy, Boomi’s Boombox ) to discuss how this iconic ballet found its footing from artistic debacle to pop culture mainstay, and how it persists in entertaining even the most cynical holiday Scrooges. Janine Kovac writes about power dynamics and women's bodies. A professional ballet dancer whose career spanned over twelve years, Janine danced with companies in San Francisco, Seattle, Iceland, Italy, and in her hometown of El Paso, Texas. Her most recent work of narrative nonfiction The Nutcracker Chronicles: A Fairytale Memoir recently received The Eyelands "Writer's Choice" Award, Greece's International Book Prize. Janine is an alumna of Hedgebrook, MacDowell, and The Mesa Refuge. She is the co-director of Litquake's Lit Crawl and curates Grotto Night for the San Francisco Public Library. Shanthi Sekaran is a novelist and television writer. Her most recent adult novel, Lucky Boy, was named a Best Book of 2017 by NPR, Barnes & Noble, and the San Francisco Chronicle. In 2021, she published her middle grade debut, The Samosa Rebellion, which won the Northern California Book Award and was named an Amazon Editor’s Pick for readers aged 9-13. Her second middle grade novel, Boomi’s Boombox , was a finalist for the California Book Award. She recently wrapped up work on the acclaimed NBC medical drama, New Amsterdam, and this spring, she'll be a Lurie Visiting Author at San Jose State University.
