87511e20-87d8-4514-932e-214e9ac39930: Jazz pianist bridging musical and artistic genres · Robert Glasper is the leader of a new sonic paradigm with a career that bridges musical and artistic genres. To date, he boasts 5 Grammy wins and 15 nominations across 9 categories, an Emmy Award for his song for Ava Duvernay’s critically hailed documentary “13th” with Common and Karriem Riggins, and a Peabody Award for his Composition of “Mr. Soul!”. His work and accolades bridge all aspects of the music business, from live touring to film scoring, composing and producing. Evolution is his hallmark. Glasper’s breakout crossover album Black Radio changed the face of the genre and set a new expectation for what popular music could be. The album won him the Grammy for Best R&B album and established him as the musician of choice for some of the world’s most iconic artists; notably playing keys throughout Kendrick Lamar's To Pimp A Butterfly, winning another Grammy for the elastic track “These Walls”. The ongoing Black Radio series has since become Glasper’s calling card, upholding a place at the heart of a trailblazing community: from long-time sonic brothers Mos Def and Bilal, to legends including Ledisi, Lupe Fiasco, Kanye West, Jill Scott, and Erykah Badu. Glasper’s eternal pursuit to further his sound has been consistent in challenging and transforming his creative horizons across the board. Whether producing a remix album with Kaytranda or as a bandleader, Robert consistently defies the limits of the genre. This is evident in a portfolio that ranges from his acoustic jazz trio, which simultaneously defies and elevates the traditional idiom by uniting it effortlessly with electronics from visionary DJ Jahi Sundance, to August Greene, a collaboration with Common + Karriem Riggins, to R+R=Now, a supergroup at the crossroads of hip-hop and Jazz. In the past year, Robert Glasper has released three diverse albums under his exclusive deal with Apple Music. The holiday album In December features artists such as Cynthia Erivo and Andra Day, while Let Go offers a calming, soulful experience that helps listeners find their center. Code Derivation merges jazz and hip-hop, with each track presented in two versions—one in jazz, and the other flipped by a producer. The track “Say Less” was flipped by Glasper’s son, Riley. Code Derivation has been nominated for a 2025 Grammy in the Best Alternative Jazz Album category. In addition to his musical accomplishments, Glasper hosted Black Radio Backstage for Tidal League, where he interviewed A-list guests like Affion Crockett, Thundercat, and Lalah Hathaway, alongside co-host Jahi Sundance. The festival he curates in Napa, The Black Radio Experience, celebrated its third year, and his legendary month-long residency at the Blue Note NYC marked its sixth season, featuring star-studded appearances from Dave Chappelle, Questlove, Marsha Ambrosius, and Andra Day, both on and off stage. Prior to a knockout 2024, in 2023 Glasper released Black Radio III and Black Radio III Supreme Edition on Loma Vista Records, with features ranging from Jennifer Hudson, Killer Mike, and the late Mac Miller. On screen, he created the original score for Run The World Season 2 and The Best Man television series. With boundless innovation and elite technique as his signature, it’s no surprise that Glasper has an avalanche of accolades, awards, and achievements to his name. Glasper is an artist at the heart of a moment - and a movement - to champion Black music, Black people, and the possibility of a better future. The hip-hop-head-nod ballad is a dedication to just that: the beauty and brilliance of a heritage that is as much Kendrick as it is Coltrane, and which seeks to empower and uplift with every offering. In his own words: “Black lives matter and so does black love; no one wants a life without love, but we have generations of people in our community who haven’t had the tools to actually be in healthy relationships. It seems like people are finally ready to open their eyes to systemic racism in this country, and if we’re going to talk about it, we have to also talk about how it affects our relationships — how we communicate, how we see ourselves, how we treat each other. It’s not always good, even though maybe it could be.” - Robert Glasper

Spotlight Sundays: Japanese American Legacies of Resistance from Program | 1–3:15 pm Post-Program Gathering | 3:15–3:45 pm All-Inclusive Ticket Join koto artist and cultural historian Shirley Kazuyo Muramoto and her son, Brian Mitsuhiro Wong , for an engaging program exploring the resilience of Japanese traditional performing arts during World War II incarceration. Through live performances, personal stories, and a presentation of instruments and other personal objects preserved from the camps, they will illuminate how Japanese American artists sustained their cultural traditions under extreme circumstances. The program will open with a traditional Japanese performance with Shirley and Brian, followed by a screening of Hidden Legacy: Japanese Traditional Performing Arts in the World War II Internment Camps , and a panel discussion moderated by Dr. Kirk Kanesaka , a kabuki actor, Japanese classical dancer, and assistant professor of Japanese and Asian Studies at California State University. Visitors are then invited to explore these historic objects and try their hand at playing a traditional Japanese instrument. This program is a part of our exhibition programming for BeHere / 1942: A New Lens on the Japanese American Incarceration on view through December 27, 2026. About Speakers and Performers Shirley Kazuyo Muramoto’s musical roots stem from her mother’s learning the koto as a child in the American prison camps of WWII. This legacy informed Shirley’s performance through the years and inspired her to research Japanese cultural arts practiced in these camps. Based in Oakland, California, she is a Master’s DaiShihan teacher by the Chikushi Kai Koto School in Fukuoka, Japan. Shirley’s has been recognized by the Hokka Nichi Bei Kai Bunka (Japanese cultural arts) Hall of Fame and Taproot Fellowship 2024, a recognition of traditional artists & culture bearers across the U.S. Her studio is in Oakland. Brian Mitsuhiro Wong represents the third generation of koto musicians in his family. He has played the koto since he was 5 years old. Brian also plays and teaches shakuhachi and shamisen. He attained his Kyoshi credential in koto instruction from the Sawai Koto Conservatory from Kazue Sawai in Tokyo with Grand Prix honors. In 2007, Brian earned his BA in Music Composition at California State University East Bay. Brian performs in the Bay Area in a variety of genres, also as part of the Golden State of Song Program talking to 4 th grade students about music in the WWII prison camps. Dr. Kirk Kanesaka is a kabuki actor, Japanese classical dancer, scholar, and Assistant Professor of Japanese and Asian Studies at California State University, San Bernardino. Recognized as the first non-Japanese professional kabuki actor, he bridges traditional Japanese arts and contemporary performance. His research explores Japanese theatre, literature, intercultural performance, and traditional aesthetics. He holds a shihan (professor’s degree) from the Bandō School of Japanese Classical Dance, performing as Bandō Hirohichirō, and is a master Japanese doll artist. In 2024, he received a Los Angeles Drama Critics Circle nomination for choreography for East West Players’ Pacific Overtures . Return to Events

But a Christmas concert with the Basie Band takes the party to another level, delivering a Santa’s sled full of swing with a program of seasonal standards over an evening show and Sunday matinee. Under the direction of trumpeter Scotty Barnhart since 2013, the orchestra staked a claim to the North Pole with 2015’s chart-topping A Very Swingin’ Basie Christmas!, the first Xmas album ever recorded by the Basie organization. The project featured special guests Ledisi, Johnny Mathis, Ellis Marsalis, and Carmen Bradford, the ebullient jazz and blues singer who continues to tour with the band. The orchestra followed up that celebratory project with a series of excellent albums, scoring GRAMMY Award nominations for 2018’s All About That Basie (with special guests Stevie Wonder, Jon Faddis, and Take 6) and 2022’s Live At Birdland, while winning a GRAMMY with 2023’s Basie Swings the Blues. For swing-loving jazz fans, there’s no better gift than a night with the Basie Orchestra.

1ceef0cc-7a37-4fc4-90dd-3dda73feacbc: The Bay Area Evolving Ground local group meets regularly at The Alembic to meditate together and explore contemporary Vajrayana. We meet and greet, then start with a short introduction to opening awareness meditation. We sit for 20 minutes, take a break, practice some slow standing meditations together, take a break, and then sit for another 20 minutes. We end with questions and discussion. Opening awareness is a seated meditation leading to vividness and spacious clarity. It is Evolving Ground’s foundational meditation and is a contemporary version of the Dzogchen practice of shi-ne (shamatha in Sanskrit). The movements come from the Sky Realm Series (Nam'khor in Tibetan). These are Dzogchen long-de practices unique to Evolving Ground. They look and feel quite similar to Qi Gong, though they operate on a different principle: discovery of the nonduality of clarity and bliss, through the experience of “tsal”—embodied awareness as non-ordinary sensation. Attendees need no prior experience. There will be plenty of space for questions, reflections, and group exploration of the practices. This meetup is free to attend. Evolving Ground is a global community exploring a transformational path of passionate involvement with the world. Our life-affirming approach empowers creative, effective individuals: people who live with courage, kindness, and grace.

f9a39c11-e532-4c7d-a5ae-ed70b7182b8b: Butoh is a slow, surreal movement practice rooted in deep listening, imagination, and transformation. In these guided movement meditations, we explore the body as landscape, myth, and memory, softening habitual patterns and awakening new ways of being. No dance experience is needed, only a curiosity and openness to move, feel, and enter the unknown. Each class begins with a gentle opening circle to arrive, ground, and set intention together. We move into a somatic warm-up, awakening sensation, breath, and subtle awareness in the body. From there, you’ll be guided through a butoh-fu score; poetic, image and/or narrative based originally written long-form prompts that invite transformation from the inside out, allowing the body to become something other than itself. We’ll also explore simple butoh exercises that deepen presence, perception, connection, and imaginative embodiment. We close with a soft landing: time to integrate, reflect, and share (if desired), leaving you resourced, expanded, and a little more in touch with the mysterious wisdom built of your body. Arrive however you are, and leave having touched something vast, intimate, and unknowably alive within you.

99bdb572-ae1e-4b1e-bb16-92e5110cb4dc: Jazz pianist bridging musical and artistic genres · Robert Glasper is the leader of a new sonic paradigm with a career that bridges musical and artistic genres. To date, he boasts 5 Grammy wins and 15 nominations across 9 categories, an Emmy Award for his song for Ava Duvernay’s critically hailed documentary “13th” with Common and Karriem Riggins, and a Peabody Award for his Composition of “Mr. Soul!”. His work and accolades bridge all aspects of the music business, from live touring to film scoring, composing and producing. Evolution is his hallmark. Glasper’s breakout crossover album Black Radio changed the face of the genre and set a new expectation for what popular music could be. The album won him the Grammy for Best R&B album and established him as the musician of choice for some of the world’s most iconic artists; notably playing keys throughout Kendrick Lamar's To Pimp A Butterfly, winning another Grammy for the elastic track “These Walls”. The ongoing Black Radio series has since become Glasper’s calling card, upholding a place at the heart of a trailblazing community: from long-time sonic brothers Mos Def and Bilal, to legends including Ledisi, Lupe Fiasco, Kanye West, Jill Scott, and Erykah Badu. Glasper’s eternal pursuit to further his sound has been consistent in challenging and transforming his creative horizons across the board. Whether producing a remix album with Kaytranda or as a bandleader, Robert consistently defies the limits of the genre. This is evident in a portfolio that ranges from his acoustic jazz trio, which simultaneously defies and elevates the traditional idiom by uniting it effortlessly with electronics from visionary DJ Jahi Sundance, to August Greene, a collaboration with Common + Karriem Riggins, to R+R=Now, a supergroup at the crossroads of hip-hop and Jazz. In the past year, Robert Glasper has released three diverse albums under his exclusive deal with Apple Music. The holiday album In December features artists such as Cynthia Erivo and Andra Day, while Let Go offers a calming, soulful experience that helps listeners find their center. Code Derivation merges jazz and hip-hop, with each track presented in two versions—one in jazz, and the other flipped by a producer. The track “Say Less” was flipped by Glasper’s son, Riley. Code Derivation has been nominated for a 2025 Grammy in the Best Alternative Jazz Album category. In addition to his musical accomplishments, Glasper hosted Black Radio Backstage for Tidal League, where he interviewed A-list guests like Affion Crockett, Thundercat, and Lalah Hathaway, alongside co-host Jahi Sundance. The festival he curates in Napa, The Black Radio Experience, celebrated its third year, and his legendary month-long residency at the Blue Note NYC marked its sixth season, featuring star-studded appearances from Dave Chappelle, Questlove, Marsha Ambrosius, and Andra Day, both on and off stage. Prior to a knockout 2024, in 2023 Glasper released Black Radio III and Black Radio III Supreme Edition on Loma Vista Records, with features ranging from Jennifer Hudson, Killer Mike, and the late Mac Miller. On screen, he created the original score for Run The World Season 2 and The Best Man television series. With boundless innovation and elite technique as his signature, it’s no surprise that Glasper has an avalanche of accolades, awards, and achievements to his name. Glasper is an artist at the heart of a moment - and a movement - to champion Black music, Black people, and the possibility of a better future. The hip-hop-head-nod ballad is a dedication to just that: the beauty and brilliance of a heritage that is as much Kendrick as it is Coltrane, and which seeks to empower and uplift with every offering. In his own words: “Black lives matter and so does black love; no one wants a life without love, but we have generations of people in our community who haven’t had the tools to actually be in healthy relationships. It seems like people are finally ready to open their eyes to systemic racism in this country, and if we’re going to talk about it, we have to also talk about how it affects our relationships — how we communicate, how we see ourselves, how we treat each other. It’s not always good, even though maybe it could be.” - Robert Glasper

c4848b17-c40f-402f-8883-6e0678c38807: Humans have been throwing parties for the winter solstice for about as long as there have been humans, from Yule to Inti Raymi to Christmas (yes, Christmas sits right on the date the old Roman calendar gave the solstice). So why all the fuss? Because the solstice is the tipping point of the year. Here in the Northern Hemisphere it's our shortest day, and it's the moment the light turns around and starts heading the other way. The light starts coming back in December, and most of us don't notice a thing until March or so. For three whole months the Earth has already picked its direction, and everything we can see still looks like the dead of winter. So much of life works exactly like that. Maybe you've got something right now that looks like it's going absolutely nowhere: a project, a relationship, a healing, a dream you keep showing up for. It may be exactly where it's supposed to be, already turned toward the light, and it's just too soon to tell. If something in your life feels like it isn't moving fast enough, this may very well be the ritual for you. We'll celebrate the return of the sun (hi, Inti!), and we'll connect with the things in our lives that are growing and moving our way, like the winter light, even if we can't see them yet. We'll strengthen our faith in the seasons of our own lives, because nothing lasts forever, but everything is always reborn. Whatever your tradition is, or if you don't have one, or if you're a little skeptical about this whole thing, you're welcome here. Bring a friend, too, because the longest night is so much better with company. If that sounds like your kind of evening, we'd love to see you there. Maritza Schäfer is a bruja, spiritual teacher, and founder of Bruja School. Raised in Chile in a family of witches, she was initiated into brujería by her grandmother. Her spiritual practice is rooted in her relationship with spirit, nature, her ancestors, and the mystery of life. Maritza has practiced magic, ritual, and divination for more than forty years, drawing on her South American and Mediterranean family lineage as well as decades of independent study and practice. She is the creator of the Liberation Magic Method, a contemporary approach to magic and spiritual practice. She is also an experienced tarot reader and teacher, having taught as part of a 150-hour, ten-month tarot certification at The Scarlet Sage in San Francisco. Alongside her spiritual work, Maritza is an organizational consultant and leadership coach who has spent her career helping leaders and organizations navigate change and transformation. Her work brings together a lifelong relationship with magic and the practical realities of work, relationships, communities, and everyday life. She brings warmth, honesty, irreverence, and humor to her teaching and ritual work.

4129f29d-f55b-4a7f-8980-2a2488083d64: Big Band Returns with Raquel Jeté: A Tribute to the Harlem Renaissance · After two sold-out headline performances, Raquel Jeté returns to Yoshi’s Oakland for her third engagement, and this holiday season she brings something new. The Harlem Standard is the debut of her newest project: an elegant evening of big band jazz that transports audiences to the Harlem Renaissance. More than a concert, The Harlem Standard is a destination. It celebrates the artistry, sophistication, and cultural legacy of one of the most influential eras in American history, when musicians, writers, and performers defined excellence for generations to come. Raquel performs her original songs reimagined in classic big band style alongside nostalgic jazz favorites, with a few special guest surprises along the way. 054bfe16-0baa-48c0-9666-9a8ab3041fde: Every Tuesday morning, the Alembic opens for a half-day of silent meditation practice. This is an unguided silent retreat consisting of three 40-minute meditation periods. There will be no teacher-led instruction during the meditation periods. Participants are invited to bring and engage in their own silent meditation practice. Whether you practice mindfulness, Zen, Vipassana, contemplation, prayer, or another silent form of meditation, all are welcome. The retreat begins promptly at 9:30 AM and concludes at 11:50 AM. Please arrive between 9:15 AM and 9:25 AM to remove your shoes, settle in, and find a seat before the first bell. The morning is divided into three periods of silent meditation: 9:30 AM – 10:10 AM 10:20 AM – 11:00 AM 11:10 AM – 11:50 AM A bell will signal the beginning and end of each meditation period. The meditation hall (Sol) is reserved for silent practice during sitting periods. Between sits, participants may quietly stretch, visit the restroom, or spend time in the tearoom. Conversation is permitted during breaks; however, we encourage participants to keep voices low, as some attendees choose to observe silence throughout the entire morning. You are welcome to leave the meditation hall at any time if needed. If you leave during a meditation period, please wait until the next break before re-entering. We ask that all entrances and exits be as quiet and unobtrusive as possible. This is a “Bring Your Own Silent Meditation” retreat. We provide the structure and the space; you provide your own silent practice. Participants may choose to sit in Sol or engage in quiet movement practice in the tearoom during meditation periods. To minimize disruption, please enter Sol only during the transition periods between sits. If you arrive after a meditation period has begun, you are welcome to practice elsewhere in the Alembic until the next bell. The suggested donation is $10. No one will be turned away for lack of funds. We do ask that all attendees register through the Momence app or via the registration link on the Alembic website. Please note that the retreat ends at 11:50 AM, and we ask all participants to depart by 12:00 PM so that our volunteer teacher and staff may close the space in a timely manner. Thank you for helping us maintain a quiet and supportive environment for practice.

2541d435-dd2c-4071-b226-6a601095b409: Plays Duke Ellington’s Nutcracker Suite featuring Tiffany Austin It’s a short walk from the SFJAZZ Center to the War Memorial Opera House, which is where the evening-length ballet The Nutcracker made its North America premiere in the winter of 1944. An immediate sensation, the production unleashed an army of Nutcrackers large and small that march across the country come the holidays, turning Tchaikovsky’s spirited score into an enchanting soundtrack for the season. In 1960, at the urging of Billy Strayhorn, the Duke Ellington Orchestra recorded The Nutcracker Suite (Columbia), a brilliant jazz interpretation of Tchaikovsky’s music. While largely forgotten today, the popular album marked a watershed in one of American music’s most consequent and productive partnerships, as Ellington gave Strayhorn equal billing for the first time on the album’s cover. For bassist, composer, and arranger Marcus Shelby, Ellington and Strayhorn’s Nutcracker Suite arrangements offer an ideal vehicle for his talent-laden New Orchestra, an ensemble he modeled after Ellington’s. Reveling in Tchaikovsky’s enduring melodies, Shelby’s band with guest vocalist Tiffany Austin breathes new life into a singular cultural fusion that gracefully marries the great Russian composer with the orchestral language of two nonpareil jazz innovators, and in addition, features original arrangements of holiday music and black spirituals.

79ff58ac-9d8b-4095-9ed9-5444e83d14f2: Embodiment Practices is an invitation to practice giving ourselves permission to arrive fully to where we are, and gently explore movement and stillness to care for our bodies and ourselves. This event happens each week at the Alembic. As an element of self attunement, we will practice making intuitive choices through a lens of self love, meaning that we are each making choices that are nourishing and responsive to ourselves as individuals in that moment. Part of this practice includes being very intentional and explicit about what kinds of choices we might consider, and being curious about how it feels to try them. There will be many options provided throughout, with guidance around how to navigate choice making, including if this is new to you or you are navigating a limitation or injury. There will be a corner of the room set aside in case you’d like to opt out of the facilitated structure and take a moment for yourself to rest. Opening Circle: We'll ground and check-in with whatever feels present for each of us. We get to welcome ourselves to come as we are. Warm Up: We'll do a guided, full-bodied warm up, tuning the instruments of our bodies and attention, giving ourselves time to shake it out, stretch, wiggle, and move through whatever feels stuck. Movements will be simple enough to follow along, giving us a chance to get out of our heads and drop into our bodies, regulating our nervous system. Drawing on contemporary dance and yoga, there will be flow, rhythm, and music. Movement Explorations: We'll explore movements that deepen our connection with our bodies and our intuition, focusing on concepts and areas of the body that can help us settle and release. Meditation: Finally, we'll settle into meditation and rest. Finding stillness might be sitting/standing/lying down and might include cozy props, having eyes open or closed, and suggestions to make yourself comfortable, including allowing some body movement within that quiet space. Please bring clothes you feel comfortable to move in. It’s recommended to bring long sleeves, long pants and socks with you, in case we are moving on the floor. Bring a journal if you’d like. Her movement style was described by The New York Times as “grounded, silken.” In addition to contemporary dance, she is currently heavily influenced by house dance, contact improvisation, and mindfulness practices. ececc128-4bc4-46f0-96b5-a9bc717b86a7: Ambassador of the Blues & Contemporary Jazz Crooner · Alvon Johnson is an internationally acclaimed vocalist, guitarist, recording artist, and entertainer whose remarkable career crosses the worlds of blues, jazz, R&B, and classic rock & roll. A defining chapter of Alvon’s career was his time as a vocalist with the world-famous, award-winning Rock & Roll Hall of Fame group The Coasters. Performing with this legendary group placed Alvon within one of the most celebrated traditions in American popular music and gave him the opportunity to perform the classic songs, comedy, and unforgettable showmanship associated with The Coasters. Today, that experience remains an important part of who Alvon Johnson is as an entertainer. Along with performing songs from his years with The Coasters, he brings audiences a sophisticated blend of blues, jazz, swing, R&B, and timeless American standards. As a Contemporary Jazz Crooner, Alvon draws inspiration from legendary vocalists including Frank Sinatra, Joe Williams, Johnny Hartman, and Nat King Cole. His guitar influences are equally distinguished, ranging from Wes Montgomery and Charlie Christian to Andrés Segovia and Jimi Hendrix. Whether fronting a small band, performing with a big band, or appearing as a solo guitarist and vocalist, Alvon has developed a style that combines musicianship, sophistication, humor, storytelling, and genuine audience connection. AMBASSADOR OF THE BLUES Alvon's deep love and respect for the blues has taken him around the world. International audiences have embraced his music, and during his performances in Russia, he has been referred to as both the “King of the Blues” and the “Ambassador of the Blues.” His international touring career has included performances throughout Russia, Spain, the United Arab Emirates , Hungary, Portugal, Poland, Malaysia, China, France, Italy, Japan, Singapore, New Zealand, Canada, The Bahamas, Australia, Africa, and other parts of Europe and the world. Throughout his career, Alvon has performed with and alongside many notable artists, including The Drifters, The Coasters, The Shirelles, Bobby Day, and Jimmie Rodgers. His musical education also came directly from some of the great figures of the blues. Alvon had opportunities to learn from and work with artists including John Lee Hooker, Pee Wee Crayton, Little Joe Blue, Harmonica Fats, Frankie Lee, Guitar Shorty, Lowell Fulson, and Buddy Ace. AN ENTERTAINER IN EVERY SENSE Music is only part of what makes an Alvon Johnson performance distinctive. Known for his natural comedic style and ability to communicate with an audience, Alvon worked with entertainers including Reynaldo Rey, Robin Harris, Skillet & Leroy, and LaWanda Page. Those experiences helped him develop the humor, timing, storytelling, and stage presence that later served him especially well during his years performing with The Coasters. That combination of music and entertainment continues to define his performances today. Alvon doesn't simply play songs—he creates an experience and develops a relationship with the audience. AWARDS & RECOGNITION Alvon Johnson's career has received numerous honors and distinctions, including: Lifetime Achievement Award — Empress Theatre of Vallejo Music Icon Award — Black Music Association & Academy of America Best Male Blues Artist — Black Music Association & Academy of America 2005 Blues Guitar Player of the Year Former vocalist with Rock & Roll Hall of Fame group The Coasters Regional winner — Guitar Center “King of the Blues” competition The Blues Grew Up — nominated for Outstanding Blues Album The Blues Grew Up — recognized among the Top 10 CDs in Japan Guitars and Cars — selected among the Top 10 CDs of 2008 by Real Blues magazine Nominated for Entertainer of the Year — International Music and Entertainment Association THE MUSIC CONTINUES From intimate wineries and jazz rooms to major festivals, concert halls, international stages, and performances with big bands, Alvon Johnson remains a uniquely versatile American entertainer. His repertoire can move effortlessly from sophisticated jazz standards and romantic ballads to swinging big-band arrangements, classic rock & roll, R&B, and guitar-driven blues. The common thread is Alvon himself: a seasoned entertainer with a deep respect for the music that shaped him and an unmistakable ability to connect with an audience. Former Vocalist with The Coasters. Contemporary Jazz Crooner. International Recording Artist. Ambassador of the Blues. Alvon Johnson — keeping the blues alive, the jazz swinging, and the spirit of classic American entertainment moving forward.

ae33359f-daf6-4fa3-8e62-e2b91c6da2c9: Raga Music on a Sunday morning with the rare, transformative beauty of a live time specific Morning Raga. In the Indian classical tradition, ragas are intimate expressions aligned with specific times of day—a concept known as samay raga . Because most modern concerts take place in the evening, hearing morning ragas performed live during their intended hours is a rarity. When done properly, the music resonates in natural harmony with the surrounding atmosphere, creating a deeply grounding and tranquil experience. Join us at Bird & Beckett Books & Records for our Monthly Morning Raga Series on Dec 27th , featuring Bansuri flutist, Akshay Naresh. Akshay Naresh is based in the San Francisco Bay Area, with more than two decades of devotion to the instrument. He trained in Hindustani classical music under Pandit Prasad Bhandarker and in Carnatic classical music under Shri Shashank, and his playing carries both traditions. He performs light music concerts, has collaborated with artists in the Bay Area, and produces music in his spare time. 6c294c0a-ceca-4fd6-a41d-3c76e6502585: 5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic. In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing. 5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you. The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives. In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach. Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

0827f8cc-8e7f-4292-8013-153812640f1b: Legendary West Coast rapper and producer · DJ Quik is a Compton, California, rapper and producer. When it comes to West Coast producers, DJ Quik is at the top of all lists. Classic albums such as Quik Is The Name (1990) and Way 2 Funky (1992) solidified DJ Quik in the ’90s Gangster Rap era of Hip Hop. Having put out several other albums since then, DJ Quik made his career producing for others. Known for his unique style of production, DJ Quik has been sought out by artists such as Jay-Z, Ludacris, Snoop Dogg, and many more to work on their projects. From a young age, Quik started to develop his musical prowess. At the age of 12, he was teaching himself how to play different instruments, and by the age of 21, he had become a multi-platinum-selling artist. After having released his first couple of albums, Quik launched his Mad Science Records label. Here, he would release Trauma (2005) and (2006), among many others that followed. Most recently, in 2016, DJ Quik put out the EP Rosecrans, a collaboration he did with Compton native rapper Problem.

Whether you practice mindfulness, Zen, Vipassana, contemplation, prayer, or another silent form of meditation, all are welcome. The retreat begins promptly at 9:30 AM and concludes at 11:50 AM. Please arrive between 9:15 AM and 9:25 AM to remove your shoes, settle in, and find a seat before the first bell. The morning is divided into three periods of silent meditation: 9:30 AM – 10:10 AM 10:20 AM – 11:00 AM 11:10 AM – 11:50 AM A bell will signal the beginning and end of each meditation period. The meditation hall (Sol) is reserved for silent practice during sitting periods. Between sits, participants may quietly stretch, visit the restroom, or spend time in the tearoom. Conversation is permitted during breaks; however, we encourage participants to keep voices low, as some attendees choose to observe silence throughout the entire morning. You are welcome to leave the meditation hall at any time if needed. If you leave during a meditation period, please wait until the next break before re-entering. We ask that all entrances and exits be as quiet and unobtrusive as possible. This is a “Bring Your Own Silent Meditation” retreat. We provide the structure and the space; you provide your own silent practice. Participants may choose to sit in Sol or engage in quiet movement practice in the tearoom during meditation periods. To minimize disruption, please enter Sol only during the transition periods between sits. If you arrive after a meditation period has begun, you are welcome to practice elsewhere in the Alembic until the next bell. The suggested donation is $10. No one will be turned away for lack of funds. We do ask that all attendees register through the Momence app or via the registration link on the Alembic website. Please note that the retreat ends at 11:50 AM, and we ask all participants to depart by 12:00 PM so that our volunteer teacher and staff may close the space in a timely manner. Thank you for helping us maintain a quiet and supportive environment for practice.
6925a9c1-e645-4325-87a7-59ee46f545fd: In this deeply experiential yoga practice, we will explore the dynamic interplay between stability and mobility, strength and relaxation, movement and stillness. Through mindful movement, standing and seated practices, breath, and attention to the subtle ways we organize ourselves in space, we'll investigate what allows us to feel both grounded and free. This event happens each week at the Alembic. Rather than striving for perfect alignment or mastering difficult poses, we'll approach the practice as an exploration. We'll slow down enough to notice, experiment with different possibilities, and discover how the balance between effort and ease can change our experience of movement — and of ourselves.. Teacher Bio: Vickie Russell Bell has been teaching yoga for more than 30 years, bringing together the precision of alignment-based yoga with a deep curiosity about how we inhabit our bodies, regulate our nervous systems, and move through the world. She is an E-RYT 500 and Certified Yoga Therapist (C-IAYT), and has studied with some of the most respected teachers in the Iyengar-influenced yoga tradition. Her teaching is grounded in the belief that yoga is less about mastering poses than developing a more intimate relationship with ourselves. Her classes invite students to slow down, pay attention, and explore the constantly shifting relationships between stability and mobility, strength and softness, effort and ease. She teaches students of all ages and abilities, with a particular interest in yoga as a practice for living fully and well over time.

f45a8094-b1bb-4a4d-bd27-1e80a948b478: KINAM es una práctica de entrenamiento psicofísico basada en la filosofía Tolteca/Anawaka (Mesoamerica antes de la colonización) y en sus antiguas posturas de equilibrio y de poder, creada a partir de diversas técnicas de movimiento funcional, meditación, y "posturas de poder toltecas". En esta clase buscamos recuperar las raíces culturales de América Prehispánica a través de la exploración de nuestra atención y consciencia y el balance de nuestros centros perceptuales: cuerpo físico, mente, emociones y energía vital. Elisa Rubio nació y creció en la Ciudad de México y se ha dedicado a la conservación ambiental y a proyectos de rematriación de tierras indígenas en CA, explorando la relación entre territorio, comunidad y naturaleza. Desde hace más de 15 años, cultiva un interés profundo por la exploración de la conciencia, la meditación y las prácticas ancestrales. En 2025 se certifico como Instructora de Kinam a través del Instituto Kinam en CDMX. Materiales a traer: Un mat de yoga o un tapete, ropa cómoda *Apto para todas las edades KINAM is a psychophysical training practice based on Toltec/Anawak (Mesoamerica before colonization) philosophy and its ancient postures of balance and power, created from various techniques of functional movement, meditation, and “Toltec power postures.” In this class, we seek to recover the cultural roots of Pre-Hispanic America through the exploration of our awareness and consciousness while balancing our perceptual centers: physical body, mind, emotions, and vital energy. Elisa Rubio was born and raised in Mexico City. Her work has focused on environmental conservation and Land Back projects in CA, exploring the relationship between land, community, and nature. For over 15 years, she has cultivated a deep interest in consciousness exploration, meditation, and ancestral practices. In 2025 she got certified by Instituto Kinam as an instructor. Materials needed : Yoga mat and comfortable clothes *All ages are welcomed
30835b87-3088-48da-8a1f-a1e39b727c02: Celebrating NYE and his NEW album "Simple Man" · Boney James — A Simple Man Three decades into a career built on deep groove, melodic instinct and a saxophone voice unmistakably his own, Boney James is still finding new ground. On A Simple Man , his milestone 20th studio album, out October 2 via Concord Records, the multi-platinum saxophonist, composer and producer delivers one of his most personal records. James’ catalog has generated more than two billion on-demand streams in the United States. His honors include four GRAMMY nominations, three NAACP Image Award nominations, four RIAA Gold-certified records and a Soul Train Award. Billboard named him one of the Top 3 Contemporary Jazz Artists of the 2000s, and in 2024 he became the first artist to score 20 No. 1 singles on the Billboard Smooth Jazz chart. Recent collaborations have also earned him two Top 10 hits at Adult R&B. For James, A Simple Man reflects a growing desire to strip away distraction and focus on what matters most. “As I’ve gotten older, I’ve realized I don’t need a lot to make me happy,” he says. “I love making music and playing my saxophone.” That clarity runs through the new album. GRAMMY-winning vocalist Ledisi joins him on the warm contemporary R&B duet “I Belong To You,” while acclaimed trumpeter Marquis Hill appears on “Morocco” and legendary guitarist Larry Carlton guests on the Steely Dan-influenced “Storybook.” James also reimagines Ellington’s “In a Sentimental Mood” over a D’Angelo-inspired groove. James’ R&B foundation runs deep. He turned professional at 19 and spent his formative years touring with Morris Day, The Isley Brothers, Teena Marie and others before stepping forward with his 1992 debut, Trust . More than three decades later, he remains focused not on preserving a legacy, but on continuing to grow. On A Simple Man, James’s playing is warmer, deeper, and stronger than ever — and, 20 albums in, he is still making progress. And that may be the clearest expression of A Simple Man : an artist who, after more than three decades, knows more clearly than ever what matters.
6c08bfd6-8ce2-47ad-998b-58c6a6f482aa: At just 21 years of age, Graham is a young gun making a name for himself in the world of Jazz today. You may find him performing under either one of his apt pseudonyms, Dud Powell or Barely Harris. (inside jazz joke!)

50bb8aa5-fd22-4d56-bbd0-094fc4150486: What better way to welcome the new year than with a blast of Cuban funk, courtesy of the man who invented the genre? Over the past decade, Cimafunk has forged a deeply soulful sound combining funk and hip-hop with rhythms from his native Cuba and other Afro-Caribbean traditions. Living in New Orleans since 2022, the dynamic vocalist dubbed his style “Afro-Cuban funk,” but that convenient label only hints at his breadth. Born in the eastern provincial capital of Pinar del Río, Erik Alejandro Iglesias Rodríguez took the first half of his stage moniker from the cimarróns, escaped slaves who lived in self-sustaining communities in colonial Cuba. He often says that his music is about freedom, and he’s fully embraced an unfettered ethos collaborating with musicians from far and wide. Whether he’s working with Cuban legends Chucho Valdés, Gonzalo Rubalcaba, and Omaru Portuando, British-Jamaican dancehall star Stylo G or the Mothership captain George Clinton himself, Cimafunk has found the universal key to unleashing bodies on the dance floor. Joined by his hard working band La Tribu, he’s recorded a series of celebrated albums, including his latest, the 2025 GRAMMY-nominated Pa' Tu Cuerpa. Returning after his showstopping performance at the 42nd San Francisco Jazz Festival in 2025, Cimafunk kicks off 2027 in spectacular style.

ca0063d0-0b7b-41cf-bbab-1211b1c3ec0f: Celebrating NYE and his NEW album "Simple Man" · Boney James — A Simple Man Three decades into a career built on deep groove, melodic instinct and a saxophone voice unmistakably his own, Boney James is still finding new ground. On A Simple Man , his milestone 20th studio album, out October 2 via Concord Records, the multi-platinum saxophonist, composer and producer delivers one of his most personal records. James’ catalog has generated more than two billion on-demand streams in the United States. His honors include four GRAMMY nominations, three NAACP Image Award nominations, four RIAA Gold-certified records and a Soul Train Award. Billboard named him one of the Top 3 Contemporary Jazz Artists of the 2000s, and in 2024 he became the first artist to score 20 No. 1 singles on the Billboard Smooth Jazz chart. Recent collaborations have also earned him two Top 10 hits at Adult R&B. For James, A Simple Man reflects a growing desire to strip away distraction and focus on what matters most. “As I’ve gotten older, I’ve realized I don’t need a lot to make me happy,” he says. “I love making music and playing my saxophone.” That clarity runs through the new album. GRAMMY-winning vocalist Ledisi joins him on the warm contemporary R&B duet “I Belong To You,” while acclaimed trumpeter Marquis Hill appears on “Morocco” and legendary guitarist Larry Carlton guests on the Steely Dan-influenced “Storybook.” James also reimagines Ellington’s “In a Sentimental Mood” over a D’Angelo-inspired groove. James’ R&B foundation runs deep. He turned professional at 19 and spent his formative years touring with Morris Day, The Isley Brothers, Teena Marie and others before stepping forward with his 1992 debut, Trust . More than three decades later, he remains focused not on preserving a legacy, but on continuing to grow. On A Simple Man, James’s playing is warmer, deeper, and stronger than ever — and, 20 albums in, he is still making progress. And that may be the clearest expression of A Simple Man : an artist who, after more than three decades, knows more clearly than ever what matters.

629abb1b-8ff3-40ea-8be4-ea0432dcf0d2: From left to right, details of works by the following artists: Brewster, Guskin, Teisl, Reyes, Tabancay, Alvarado, Ratcliff, Lisch, Biagini, Alaverdi, Perillo, Weiss, McLennan, Rosenberg For twenty years, Mercury Twenty Gallery has been a vital part of Oakland’s arts community. Founded on Grand Avenue in 2006 and relocating to 25th Street in 2009, the gallery has sustained a thriving artist-run business with a commitment to artistic independence. Mercury Twenty has built an extensive network of artists—21 current members and more than 60 alumni—who together have shaped Oakland’s creative landscape. Gallery members played a role in the early development of Oakland Art Murmur and helped establish the 25th Street arts district. Through two decades of artistic exploration and collaboration, Mercury Twenty is a vibrant and enduring presence in Oakland’s cultural life. For this milestone exhibition, current members and participating alumni have been organized into small curatorial teams. Thoughtfully assembled, these groups bring together different artistic perspectives and practices, creating unexpected visual connections and engaging conversations between works. c21fcf9c-c536-419a-8f71-ef22c1940725: Many of us work with psychedelics without a guide or with limited support to integrate these experiences. That can feel painful or lonely when we’ve had meaningful journeys (and also when we’ve had disappointing journeys!). Healing – especially from interpersonal injuries – deepens when done in community. The same is true of personal and spiritual growth. Even the most joyful experiences are best metabolized when witnessed. Together, we become a mosaic – a colorful and varied community, greater together than the sum of our parts. Mosaic is a psychedelic integration circle for self-identified women. Here, you’ll find a supportive space to integrate the lessons, challenges, and wisdom from psychedelic journeys so that you can apply those learnings to everyday life. Together, we’ll seek to understand our psychedelic experiences and make profound insights accessible and actionable. Please arrive 10 minutes early to get settled in. We’ll begin promptly at the scheduled start time and cannot accommodate late arrivals. Thank you for helping us create a smooth experience for everyone. This is a drop-in, monthly supported peer group rather than a psychotherapy group. We create space for sharing stories and experiences, receiving support, and forging genuine connections. Meditation, mindful movement, somatic practices, Internal Family Systems parts work, and creative tools are all part of the fun. Whether you’re new to integration or looking to deepen your practice, you’ll find a supportive community here. Note: You’re invited to bring an object for our community altar that represents some aspect of your journey. No one turned away for lack of funds. If this applies to you, please pay at the door. This event is a closed container. There will be no further entry after 2:15. Dr. Lyssa Menard is a psychologist, psychedelic therapist, and professor (Northwestern University Medical School) with specialties in Integrative Medicine, trauma treatment, and health psychology. She is the founder of Strategies for Change, a coaching and consulting firm promoting personal, organizational, and leadership change and has been a consultant to a wide range of media outlets, including CNN, New York Times, and WebMD. She brings this varied background to her integration groups, facilitating growth and change through a multi-media concoction of integrative therapeutic approaches (mindful movement, creative arts, somatic healing and embodiment, social connection, and spiritual ritual). Dr. Menard’s book, "Results May Vary: Hope & Healing through Psychedelic-assisted Psychotherapy" is scheduled for release in 2026. As a beneficiary of excellent (and also, sadly, lackluster) psychedelic treatment, she is a skeptic of the field, a critic when necessary, and a true believer in the healing possibilities offered by these medicines. She serves as an advocate for community and patient education and fights for legal access to psychedelics for health and healing. As a recent transplant to California's Bay Area, Dr. Menard spends a ridiculous amount of time at The Berkeley Alembic, cavorting in nature, worshipping the sun, and developing community. cd5af092-51fe-4acd-8e0a-87d935994af3: Featuring Nate’ THESOULSANGER & Mirraje · Two powerful women. Two distinctive voices. One soulful night of music. NATE’ THESOULSANGER Some artists find their voice. Nate’ THESOULSANGER inherited hers. Born and raised in Oakland, Nate’ comes from a rich musical heritage as a descendant of the Grammy-winning Gospel Hummingbirds . Raised in a legacy of faith, storytelling, and soul, music was never simply something she discovered it was part of her foundation. An award-winning vocalist, international recording artist, songwriter, producer, actress, event host, and co-founder of SoulGlo Productions, LLC , THESOULSANGER has built a career that refuses to be confined to one genre. Her sound moves through soul, gospel, R&B, hip hop, theater, and beyond , bringing authenticity, power, and unmistakable Oakland soul to every performance. Throughout her career, she has shared stages and studios with artists including Patti LaBelle, Kelly Price, Carlos Santana, MC Hammer, LaRussell , and Grammy-winning producer Narada Michael Walden , with whom she has developed a longstanding creative relationship. Her voice is also woven into Bay Area music history. Nate’ created and recorded the memorable hook for Mac Dre’s “Make You Mine,” a song that became part of his enduring musical legacy. Her credits span radio, film, theater, live production, and recording. A Bay Area Rising Star and Best Vocalist award recipient , she has received KMEL airplay, contributed vocals to the Warner Bros. film The Invasion , and established herself as a trusted creative force both onstage and behind the scenes. At Yoshi’s Oakland , Nate’ has become such a familiar presence as a headliner, host, featured vocalist, producer, and collaborator that she earned the affectionate nickname “Ms. Yoshi’s.” Whether singing, producing, acting, hosting, mentoring, or creating opportunities for others, Nate’ brings the same qualities to every room: authenticity, excellence, soul, and connection. Singer. Songwriter. Producer. Actress. Host. Mentor. Community Builder. Oakland soul in every room she enters. Nate’ THESOULSANGER. The THE is intentional. CHRISTIE “MIRRAJE” MALONE Christie “Mirraje” Malone was born to sing. The daughter of blues musician George “Bluestone” Malone , Mirraje began singing at the age of three and writing songs and poetry by age nine. A gifted singer, songwriter, and natural stage performer, music has been woven into her life from the very beginning. Growing up in Los Angeles, Mirraje’s journey has been shaped by love, loss, perseverance, and an unwavering desire to create. After caring for her mother and experiencing her passing, Mirraje stepped away from singing and writing for four years. The memory of her mother—her greatest inspiration, biggest fan, and loudest cheerleader—eventually reignited her passion and gave her the courage to dream and create again. As she embarked upon her solo career, Mirraje recognized the extraordinary musical journey that had already taken shape. She has shared the stage with celebrated artists including Stevie Wonder, Evelyn “Champagne” King, Morris Day, Zapp, Club Nouveau, Cameo, Sugar Hill Gang, and Klymaxx . Mirraje’s musical influences span genres and generations, with Anita Baker holding a special place among her favorites. Her eclectic love of music allows her to find inspiration in the experiences, thoughts, emotions, and sounds that surround her. Rather than allowing her artistry to be defined by a particular genre or category, Mirraje creates from a place of freedom and authenticity. In her own words: “Life is unpredictable and unique. It should never be defined by genres or categories; nor should our music be. I just do what feels good.” SANG SIS! Together, Nate’ THESOULSANGER and Christie “Mirraje” Malone bring two extraordinary musical journeys to one stage for SANG SIS! —a celebration of powerful women, authentic voices, soulful storytelling, and music that refuses to be put in a box. 06124977-5269-46ab-804e-e1c19b4260e6: Psychedelics can surface anything, including awe, insight, grief, trauma, even ancestral or collective pain. Without support, it can be hard to make sense of what happened, let alone carry it forward in a meaningful way. Yirah—often translated as awe, reverence, or a kind of holy trembling—is the feeling of standing at the edge of something vast, meaningful, and not entirely knowable. Psychedelic experiences often bring us right to that edge. This Jewish psychedelic integration circle offers a space to meet those moments together, within the safety of Jewish community and the container of Jewish teachings. Together, we make meaning of what we’ve seen and felt, and begin the slow, human work of weaving those insights into our lives. Please arrive 10 minutes early to get settled in. We’ll begin promptly at the scheduled start time and cannot accommodate late arrivals. Thank you for helping us create a smooth experience for everyone. Each monthly, drop-in circle includes grounding and intention-setting, a brief orientation, an experiential practice (meditation, movement, somatic work, or parts work), and small- and large-group sharing. This is a supported peer group rather than psychotherapy, designed to foster connection, reflection, and practical integration. Note: This is an affinity space exclusively for people who identify as Jewish—by heritage or conversion—including those who are part-Jewish. Those who do not meet these criteria will not be admitted. To support safety and connection in a time of deep division, we also hold a clear and intentional container: we do not engage in political discussion here. The focus is on integration, presence, and community. Whether you’re new to Jewish practice or finding your way back in, whether your journeys have been expansive, messy, or disorienting—you’re welcome here. Facilitator Bio: Lyssa Menard, PhD, is a clinical psychologist, psychedelic therapist, and professor at Northwestern University Medical School who specializes in trauma, integrative medicine, and what it actually takes to change. She’s been featured in places like CNN and The New York Times, but her real work happens in circles like this one—where people show up as they are and do the brave, uncomfortable, life-changing work of integration. Jewish by birth and in a more recent, intentional deep dive into Jewish life, Lyssa brings a deep respect for tradition alongside a willingness to question, wrestle, and reinterpret—in the long Jewish tradition of meaning-making. After all, Israel can be translated as “one who wrestles with God.” Her relationship to psychedelics is both professional and personal. She’s experienced their power, their limitations, and everything in between—which makes her equal parts skeptic and believer.

e9a016ef-e7d2-46a8-93d3-a7e3d747509f: Topic and guest to be announced. The Chalice is a recurring psychedelic salon held at the Berkeley Alembic the first Wednesday of every month. Instead of the mainstream focus on clinical trials, legal frameworks, and psychotherapy, the Chalice will draw from the deeper humanistic wells of history, poetry, the gods, ethnobotany, humor, and mystery. We are less interested in fetishizing psychedelic substances or psychedelic experiences than in cultivating psychedelic culture and exploring what it means to be psychedelic people. This first half of this event will be streamed online. The co-hosts for Chalice are Erik Davis, author and Alembic co-founder; Maria Mangini, co-founder of the Women’s Visionary Council and old-school head; and Christian Greer, currently a lecturer on counterculture at Stanford University. The first half of each gathering will feature a talk or special guest interview; the second half of the evening is designed to develop the community, sometimes with breakout groups, story hours, and peer-to-peer discussion, and always with more questions than answers. J. Christian Greer, PhD, is a scholar of Religious Studies with a special focus on global psychedelic culture. He has held teaching positions at Harvard University, Yale University, and is currently a lecturer at Stanford's Medical School. He is the co-founder, and the co-chair of the Drugs and Religion program unit at the American Academy of Religion, and each June, he leads “The Psychedelic Universe: Global Perspectives on Higher Consciousness,” an intensive, 2-week seminar on the history of psychedelics, hosted on-location at the University of Amsterdam, Netherlands. Alongside his research, he is an organizer for the Order of St. George's Horse, a pilgrimage confraternity & book publisher. His latest books include, Void Machines: the Paper Shrines of J. Christian Greer is a collection of his artwork, and Kumano Kodo: Pilgrimage to Powerspots (co-authored with Dr. Michelle Oing) which analyzes the pilgrimage folklore associated with the rainforests of Japan's Kii Peninsula. Learn more about his work here: orderofstgeorgeshorse.com Erik Davis, PhD, is an author, award-winning journalist, and teacher based in San Francisco. His wide-ranging work focuses on alternative religion, media culture, the popular imagination, and the psychedelic underground. He is the author of High Weirdness: Drugs, Esoterica, and Visionary Experience in the Seventies (2019); Nomad Codes: Adventures in Modern Esoterica (2010); The Visionary State: A Journey through California’s Spiritual Landscape (2006), a critical volume on Led Zeppelin (2005), and the celebrated cult classic TechGnosis: Myth, Magic, and Mysticism in the Age of Information (1998), which remains in print. Davis’s scholarly and popular essays on music, technoculture, drugs, and spirituality have appeared in scores of books, magazines, and journals, and his writing has been translated into a dozen languages. Davis has spoken widely at universities, conferences, retreat centers, and festivals, and has been interviewed by CNN, the BBC, NPR, and the New York Times. He graduated from Yale University in 1988, and earned his PhD in religious studies at Rice University in 2015. He writes the online publication the Burning Shore (www.burningshore.com), and his next book is Blotter: the Untold Story of an Acid Medium (2024).www.techgnosis.com Mariavittoria Mangini, PhD, FNP has written extensively on the impact of psychedelic experiences in shaping the lives of her contemporaries, and has worked closely with many of the most distinguished investigators in this field. She is one of the founders of the Women’s Visionary Council, a nonprofit organization that supports investigations into non-ordinary forms of consciousness and organizes gatherings of researchers, healers, artists, and activists whose work explores these states. She is a visiting scholar at the Berkeley Center for the Science of Psychedelics, and Professor Emerita in the School of Science, Allied Health, and Nursing at Holy Names University. For the last 50 years, she has been a part of the Hog Farm, a well-known communal family based in Berkeley and in Laytonville, California.
1ece4fbf-9068-42ab-97c8-4653c1236d43: FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation, $49 with signed book Co-presented with Grace Cathedral’s The Forum Interweaving memoir and good old fashioned ice adventure, Kim Stanley Robinson’s latest takes readers along on the journeys that have happened before and those that may never happen again. In May of 1911, Robert Scott and his men said goodbye to the sun and settled in for the long Antarctic winter. When the sun returned in September, they would try to become the first people to reach the South Pole. However, a week past the winter solstice, Scott’s second-in-command decided to take an impromptu sled trip. Chronicled by zoological assistant Apsley Cherry-Garrard, this side trip became The Worst Journey in the World, one of the best adventure books ever written. Robinson first read Cherry-Garrard’s book in his twenties and re-read it again in 1995, as preparation for a research trip to Antarctica for his Mars novels. It was a dream excursion: he traveled around the continent, by snowmobile and helicopter and airplane, and followed in their ill-fated footsteps. Doors at 7:00 PM.
9fc07104-8ef7-4fea-8657-22ca3e284fc2: One of the world’s preeminent jazz innovators, trombonist and seashellist Steve Turre, has consistently won both the Readers’ and Critics’ polls in JazzTimes, Downbeat, and Jazziz for Best Trombone and for Best Miscellaneous Instrumentalist (shells). Turre was born to Mexican-American parents and grew up in the San Francisco Bay Area, where he absorbed daily doses of mariachi, blues, and jazz. While attending Sacramento State University, he joined the Escovedo Brothers salsa band, which began his career-long involvement with that genre. In 1972, Steve Turre’s career picked up momentum when Ray Charles hired him to go on tour. A year later, Turre’s mentor Woody Shaw brought him into Art Blakey’s Jazz Messengers. After his tenure with Blakey, Turre went on to work with a diverse list of musicians from the jazz, Latin, and pop worlds, including Dizzy Gillespie, McCoy Tyner, J.J. Johnson, Herbie Hancock, Lester Bowie, Tito Puente, Mongo Santamaria, Van Morrison, Pharoah Sanders, Horace Silver, Max Roach, and Rahsaan Roland Kirk. The latter introduced a hum to the seashell as an instrument. Soon after that, while touring in Mexico City with Woody Shaw, Turre’s relatives informed him that his ancestors similarly played the shells. Since then, Turre has incorporated seashells into his diverse musical style. In addition to performing as a member of the Saturday Night Live Band since 1984, Turre leads several different ensembles. Sanctified Shells utilizes the seashell in a larger context, transforming his horn section into a “shell choir”. Turre’s Spring 1999 Verve release, Lotus Flower, showcases his Sextet With Strings. The recording explores many great standards and original compositions arranged by Turre for a unique instrumentation of trombone and shells, violin, cello, piano, bass, and drums. Turre’s quartet and quintet provide a setting based in tradition and stretching the limits conceptually and stylistically. In the Summer of 2000, Telarc released In the Spur of the Moment. This recording features Steve with three different quartets, each with a different and distinct master pianist: Ray Charles, Chucho Valdes, and Stephen Scott. Turre’s self-titled Verve release pioneers a unique artistic vision, drawing upon jazz, Afro-Cuban, and Brazilian sources. This innovative recording also features Cassandra Wilson, Randy Brecker, Graciela, Mongo Santamaria, and J.J. Johnson. Previously, Turre recorded Right There and Rhythm Within, featuring Herbie Hancock, Jon Faddis, Pharoah Sanders, and Sanctified Shells, on Verve’s subsidiary label, Antilles. Steve Turre continually evolves as a musician and arranger. He has a strong command of all musical genres, and when it comes to his distinct brand of jazz, he always keeps one foot in the past and one in the future.

f49b3d08-ac3f-48ff-b09d-8d7d58bab289: Embodiment Practices is an invitation to practice giving ourselves permission to arrive fully to where we are, and gently explore movement and stillness to care for our bodies and ourselves. This event happens each week at the Alembic. As an element of self attunement, we will practice making intuitive choices through a lens of self love, meaning that we are each making choices that are nourishing and responsive to ourselves as individuals in that moment. Part of this practice includes being very intentional and explicit about what kinds of choices we might consider, and being curious about how it feels to try them. There will be many options provided throughout, with guidance around how to navigate choice making, including if this is new to you or you are navigating a limitation or injury. There will be a corner of the room set aside in case you’d like to opt out of the facilitated structure and take a moment for yourself to rest. Opening Circle: We'll ground and check-in with whatever feels present for each of us. We get to welcome ourselves to come as we are. Warm Up: We'll do a guided, full-bodied warm up, tuning the instruments of our bodies and attention, giving ourselves time to shake it out, stretch, wiggle, and move through whatever feels stuck. Movements will be simple enough to follow along, giving us a chance to get out of our heads and drop into our bodies, regulating our nervous system. Drawing on contemporary dance and yoga, there will be flow, rhythm, and music. Movement Explorations: We'll explore movements that deepen our connection with our bodies and our intuition, focusing on concepts and areas of the body that can help us settle and release. Meditation: Finally, we'll settle into meditation and rest. Finding stillness might be sitting/standing/lying down and might include cozy props, having eyes open or closed, and suggestions to make yourself comfortable, including allowing some body movement within that quiet space. Please bring clothes you feel comfortable to move in. It’s recommended to bring long sleeves, long pants and socks with you, in case we are moving on the floor. Bring a journal if you’d like. About Suzanne (Zan): With three decades of contemporary/modern dance experience and 15 years of teaching, Suzanne Beahrs guides students in exploring movement as a pathway to deeper connection—with ourselves, our surroundings, and each other. Her classes blend technical training, creative expression, and guidance on being intentional with how we are each practicing. Her movement style was described by The New York Times as “grounded, silken.” In addition to contemporary dance, she is currently heavily influenced by house dance, contact improvisation, and mindfulness practices. She is currently on faculty at Shawl-Anderson Dance Center and teaches around the Bay Area, including ODC, the Berkeley Alembic, and Finnish Hall. Zan has previously taught extensively at Gibney, Elon University, ADF studios, and many more. She has shown her choreography in NY, NC, CA, AZ, MA, and MO, and performed in works by Ishika Seth, Mo Miner, and others. Beyond the studio, Suzanne is a facilitator and has worked as a DEI consultant. She also enjoys exploring writing, visual art, nature, music, and belonging. Education: MFA in Dance, NYU Tisch School of the Arts; BA in Geology, UC Berkeley Learn more about Suzanne, upcoming classes/workshops (contemporary, embodiment, improvisation, contact improvisation and private lessons): IG @suzannebeahrs suzannebeahrs.com

7e22ade2-c9f9-4c07-8df2-cae8d2d83390: Award-winning guitar virtuoso and blues singer · " One of the most prodigious and gifted electric bluesmen on the planet...a deeply soulful singer and incendiary guitarist [with] a seemingly endless penchant for invention." –AllMusic "Smoking songs and heavy-hitting guitar full of fire and passion...Montoya’s rough-edged voice is filled with feeling. Bluesy, powerful and unpredictable...[It]really gets the blood flowing." –Blues Music Magazine "Montoya is a show-stopper...heartfelt singing and merciless guitar with a wicked icy burn. He is one of the truly gifted blues artists of his generation." –Living Blues “’Just play what you feel, be real about it, and enjoy yourself.’ That’s what Albert Collins taught me,” says the award-winning guitar virtuoso and soul-deep singer Coco Montoya. The self-taught, left-handed Montoya mastered his craft under Collins’ tutelage. Incorporating lessons learned from his mentors, the iconic Collins (for whom he originally drummed), and UK legend John Mayall, Montoya puts his own stamp on every song he performs. Since his first solo album in 1995 (which won him the Blues Music Award for Best New Artist), Montoya’s endlessly inventive guitar work and passionate, hard-hitting vocals have kept him at the top of the blues world. With his new Alligator Records album, Writing On The Wall (his sixth for the label), Montoya delivers what he is already calling one of the best records he’s ever made. For the very first time on Alligator, he decided to bring his road-tested band—noted keyboardist and songwriter Jeff Paris (Keb’ Mo’, Bill Withers), bassist Nathan Brown, and drummer Rena Beavers—into the studio with him. Between the camaraderie of the long-time bandmates and the sheer talent of all involved, the results have left Coco, in his words, “over the moon.” Produced by Grammy Award-winner Tony Braunagel (Bonnie Raitt, Taj Mahal) and co-produced by Jeff Paris, Writing On The Wall is a tour-de-force of memorable, hook-filled songs, sung with passion and fueled by equally memorable, top-shelf musicianship. The 13 tracks include five written or co-written by Montoya. The set opens with a signature, career-defining performance of the soul-baring I Was Wrong , written for Coco by songwriter Dave Steen. From the blistering Save It For The Next Fool to the enjoy now/pay later philosophy of Jeff Paris’ (I’d Rather Feel) Bad About Doin’ It to the riveting reinvention of Lonnie Mack’s Stop , Montoya delivers each song with heart-pounding emotion. Special guest Lee Roy Parnell adds his well-seasoned slide guitar to the smoldering A Chip And A Chair . And Coco’s friend, guitarist Ronnie Baker Brooks (son of late Alligator star Lonnie Brooks), joins in for some good-natured fun on the droll Baby, You’re A Drag and adds his blistering playing to the searing cover of Bobby Bland’s You Got Me. “I am so proud of this one,” Montoya says of Writing On The Wall . “We recorded in Jeff Paris’ studio, and everything just gelled together. And the band inspired me; they all gave extra effort at every turn. Jeff, Nathan and Rena played so great, they ended up making me play even harder. They made me sound better than I am!” Henry “Coco” Montoya was born in Santa Monica, California, on October 2, 1951, and raised in a working-class family. Growing up, Coco immersed himself in his parents’ record collection. He listened to big band jazz, salsa, doo-wop and rock ‘n’ roll. His first love was drums; he acquired a kit at age 11. He got a guitar two years later. “I’m sure the Beatles had something to do with this,” Montoya recalls. “I wanted to make notes as well as beats.” But guitar was his secondary instrument. Montoya turned his love of drumming into his profession, playing in a number of area rock bands while still in his teens and becoming an in-demand drummer. In 1969, Montoya saw Albert King opening a Creedence Clearwater Revival/Iron Butterfly concert at the Shrine Auditorium in Los Angeles. He was transformed. “After King got done playing,” says Montoya, “my life was changed. When he played, the music went right into my soul. It grabbed me so emotionally that I had tears welling up in my eyes. Nothing had ever affected me to this level. He showed me what music and playing the blues were all about. I knew that was what I wanted to do.” The next chapter of Montoya’s story was kick-started by a chance meeting in the mid-1970s with legendary bluesman Albert Collins. Montoya says, “Albert was coming through Los Angeles and needed to borrow my drum set, which I left at the club where he was going to be playing. I went down to see his show that night, and it just tore my head off. The thing that I had seen and felt with Albert King came pouring back on me when I saw Albert Collins.” A short time later, Collins hired Montoya as his band’s drummer. With Albert mentoring Coco on the guitar during the band’s downtime, Coco soon became Collins’ second guitarist. “We’d sit in hotel rooms for hours and play guitar,” remembers Montoya. “He’d play that beautiful rhythm of his and just have me play along. He was always saying, ‘Don’t think about it, just feel it.’ He was like a father to me,” says Coco, who often slept at Collins’ home. When Collins declared Montoya his “son,” it was the highest praise and affection he could offer. In return, Montoya learned everything he could from the legendary Master of the Telecaster. Needing a more regular paycheck, Montoya left Collins’ band after two years and took a job tending bar, jamming on weekends at Los Angeles clubs. One day, legendary British musician John Mayall heard Coco playing Otis Rush’s All Your Love (I Miss Loving) onstage. Soon after, Mayall called on Montoya to join his famous Bluesbreakers. Filling the shoes of previous Bluesbreakers guitarists Eric Clapton, Peter Green and Mick Taylor would not be easy, but Montoya knew he could not pass up the opportunity to play with another legend. For the next ten years he toured the world and recorded with Mayall on seven albums, soaking up the experience of life on the road and in the recording studio. Montoya’s recorded debut as a bandleader came with 1995’s Gotta Mind To Travel (originally on Silvertone Records in England and later issued in the USA on Blind Pig Records). The album became an instant fan favorite. Blues enthusiasts, radio programmers, and critics sent praise from all corners. The album immediately made it clear that Montoya ranked among the best players on the contemporary scene. Two more Blind Pig albums followed, and Coco was well on his way. In 2000, Montoya’s Alligator debut, Suspicion , quickly became the best-selling album of his career, earning regular radio airplay on over 120 stations nationwide. Montoya’s fan base exploded. After two more highly successful and massively popular Alligator releases—2002’s Can’t Look Back and 2007’s Dirty Deal —Montoya signed with Ruf Records, cutting both a live and a studio album. Returning to Alligator with 2017’s Hard Truth and 2019’s Coming In Hot , the guitar master continued to blaze his trail. “Montoya unleashes one career-topping performance after another,” declared the UK’s Blues Matters . Still an indefatigable road warrior, Montoya continues to tour virtually nonstop, bringing audiences to their feet from New York to New Orleans to Chicago to San Francisco. Across the globe, he’s performed in countries including Australia, Belgium, Switzerland, Germany, Norway, England, Brazil, Argentina, Spain, Mexico, Ecuador, Italy, Poland, Russia, the Czech Republic and Canada. Now, with the dynamic Writing On The Wall and a tour calendar busting at the seams, Coco Montoya is as excited as he’s ever been to perform the new songs live with his burning-hot band. Montoya’s well-earned reputation as an eye-popping live performer precedes him. Vintage Guitar states, “Coco keeps getting better and better. He plays with fire and passion rarely seen in this day and age.” Billboard declares, “In a world of blues guitar pretenders, Coco Montoya is the real McCoy. He exudes power and authenticity. Be prepared to get scorched by the real thing.”

d7e86143-7292-47d3-952c-b87c5a8ae508: Experience the deep benefits of Zhineng (Wisdom Healing) Qigong. This practice strengthens the immune system, supports the body’s natural capacity to heal, and cultivates mental clarity and emotional steadiness. Through simple, time-honored movements, the nervous system unwinds, the mind becomes more spacious, and the heart opens. Over time, practitioners often feel more resilient, centered, and connected — both inwardly and outwardly. Tickets are sliding scale $10-$25 - Please arrive at least 5-10 minutes early. Hiromi Vardy is a certified Zen Shiatsu, Yang style Tai Chi, and Zhineng Qigong healer and practitioner. She first encountered Tai Chi in 1973 while studying theater design and performance art in London. Initially drawn to the beauty of the movements, she soon discovered that the practice had a profound effect on her consciousness, awakening a deep interest in the healing arts. While collaborating on stage with dancers in London, Hiromi began treating injuries in overworked bodies. In 1976, after a serious accident that resulted in loss of circulation in her leg and concern about possible amputation, she turned to daily Tai Chi practice, self-massage, and treatment from a Japanese acupuncturist. This experience became a turning point in her healing journey and led her back to Japan, where she studied Shiatsu at the Namikoshi School and trained at the Zen Shiatsu Center under Shizuto Masunaga. After moving to the United States with her family in 1987, Hiromi continued deepening her practice and teaching. During a period of significant stress later in her life, she encountered Master Ming Tong Gu and began studying Zhineng (wisdom healing) Qigong under his guidance, eventually becoming licensed to teach. The healing shift she experienced through this practice was profound and continues to inform her teaching today. Since 2013, Hiromi has been dedicated to teaching Zhineng Qigong, expanding her offerings to include online classes in 2020. Her work invites students to explore the foundations of Qigong and Tai Chi as embodied, healing practices that cultivate awareness, vitality, and resilience.
