d5300904-a501-42f1-8873-c14d478f34d5: In recent years, the most vital, inclusive, and innovative jazz scene on earth has shifted east across the Atlantic to London, and the figure that stands atop this revolution is Shabaka (formerly known as Shabaka Hutchings). The former leader of the heralded conglomerations Sons of Kemet, Shabaka and the Ancestors, and The Comet is Coming, Shabaka returns to SFJAZZ with music from his 2026 release Of the Earth — an innovative and adventurous solo recording that marks both his return to the saxophone and his immersion into electronic beats and loops that has opened new worlds for exploration. A multi-faceted instrumentalist and composer whose influence has spread far beyond the U.K., the Birmingham-raised Hutchings spent the formative years of his youth in Barbados, an island rife with reminders of Britain’s colonial history, where the budding artist first picked up the saxophone and where the seeds of his creative aesthetic in the roots of the African diaspora were planted. Bristling with raw energy and deep spiritual power, Of the Earth was inspired by the solo producer-auteur approach of the late D’Angelo and points to Shabaka’s vision for his future relationship with the instrument, allowing him to fully embrace new sonic realms and chart new expressive paths, each marked by resonances from the ancient past while feeling resolutely of the moment. Personnel: Shabaka (tenor saxophone, flute, electronics)

f3f07dce-60a5-4fb2-a3ef-b199c3ca1009: Creative expression is a way to integrate phenomenon and visions experienced in altered states of consciousness, whether they be meditative or entheogenic in nature. From the very first forms of mark-making to the caves of Lascaux to the works of Pablo Amaringo and Alex Grey, humanity has sought to understand our internal landscapes through visual expression. Alligator Lizards in the Air: Healing and Integration through Creative Expression, is a once a month chance to bring these experiences to life through two dimensional mark making. Art mediums from paint to colored pencils, crayons to markers, will be available for everyone to use along with paper and canvas. Krisztina Lazar will be your visionary guide in creativity and will help you realize your experience before your eyes. No art background needed for this class. All you need is an open mind and a willingness to explore. No one turned away for lack of funds. If this applies to you, please email hello@berkeleyalembic.org at least 48 hours before the event start. Krisztina Lazar is a visionary artist primarily working in oil paint, watercolor and drawing. She is a Mische Technique lineage holder, a mixture of oil and egg tempera painting invented during the Dutch Renaissance and revolutionized by modern master, Ernst Fuchs. This technique creates an opalescent under painting that the colors are then glazed over, rendering each painting out of light rather than shadow, bringing the images to life with fractal clarity. Utilizing this transformative style that she learned from visionary pioneer, Brigid Marlin, her current body of work explores painting a hybrid of Mische and Alla Prima to render hyperealistic sacred art. With these two techniques combined, Krisztina creates images of Pop Shamanism, portals and visions that speak to today’s cultural climate of the occult, magic, fantasy, psychedelics, meditation, pop, nostalgia, and the environment movement. Originally from Cleveland, OH, she completed her BFA at Carnegie Mellon University in 2004 and her MFA graduate degree in 2011 at the San Francisco Art Institute New Genres department. Her paintings have been exhibited in group and solo shows throughout the United States and Europe, most notably at the H.R. Geiger museum in Gruyere, Switzerland. She teaches her unique styles of painting to many students in group and private settings. Her work has been featured in multiple articles, galleries and book publications. She currently lives and works in Northern California.

e3ec69d8-7acf-4ef8-8536-db69e905c6bb: Aga Khan Master Musicians is a collective spanning traditions from the Mediterranean to Asia. The lineup: Wu Man is a world-leading player on the pipa (Chinese lute), Syrian-born Basel Rajoub has developed an entirely new repertoire for the saxophone, Feras Charestan is a master of the qanun (Middle-Eastern zither), Yurdal Tokcan is an authority on oud (Turkish lute), and Uzbek Abbos Kosimov is a virtuoso on the doira (Uzbek frame drum). Together they reveal a collection of jointly-created works inspired by ancient trade routes and enduring cross-cultural connections.

d2049bf5-d9c7-4b25-b072-bb365709328b: 5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic. In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing. 5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you. The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives. In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach. Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

340dfeb3-61dd-4e09-8192-6b494e21e0fa: Beginning in 1992, when his group New Klezmer Trio “kicked open the door for radical experiments with Ashkenazi roots music” (SF Chronicle), clarinetist Ben Goldberg has established himself as “one of the most vibrant, flexible, and inventive clarinetists in jazz and improvised music” (Downbeat). NPR calls Ben “an artist who seems to find beautiful melodies at the end of every path,” and The New York Times has noted his music for “a feeling of joyous research into the basics of polyphony and collective improvising.” After twice being named Rising Star Clarinetist in the Downbeat Critics Poll, he now consistently places in the top two in the Clarinet category. Ben has received grants from the National Endowment for the Arts, Chamber Music America, and the Shifting Foundation. Ben has released over forty albums of his original music, including Go Home, “a searching ensemble that welcomes lyrical improvisation while embracing the groove” (The New Yorker); Orphic Machine, a song-cycle with lyrics from Allen Grossman’s speculative poetics — “knotted and occasionally spooky composition marked by dazzling interplay” (LA Times); and Everything Happens To Be, which All About Jazz said “seems to come from a place outside of time – or maybe it comes from several times simultaneously.”

26ae5438-5956-4b24-b00e-aa4cedc53cc7: w/ Melissa Aldana, Linda May Han Oh, & Jeff “Tain” Watts “The titan among us,” (DownBeat), GRAMMY Award-winning saxophonist Joe Lovano is one of the era’s definitive improvisers and bandleaders and brings a remarkable group of the most accomplished instrumentalists in jazz to SFJAZZ for these two nights. John Coltrane famously described his musical journey to fellow legend Wayne Shorter as “starting a sentence in the middle and then going to the beginning and the end of it at the same time…both directions at once." To help commemorate one of this season’s themes, celebrating the centennial of John Coltrane, Lovano presides over a staggering band of all-stars including saxophonist Melissa Aldana, bassist Linda May Han Oh, and drummer Jeff “Tain” Watts for a project he calls “Both Directions at Once.” Winner of the 2013 Thelonious Monk International Saxophone Competition, GRAMMY nominee Melissa Aldana was named to DownBeat’s “25 For the Future” list in 2016 and has released eight albums including 2026’s Filin. A veteran of work with Pay Metheny, Vijay Iyer, and Dave Douglas, Linda May Han Oh has released five albums and was voted Bassist of the Year by JazzTimes, Hothouse, and the Jazz Journalists Association. Among the most influential drummers in jazz history, Jeff “Tain” Watts is a powerhouse artist best known for his long-term work with Branford and Wynton Marsalis, Kenny Garrett, and his own incendiary releases. Personnel: Joe Lovano tenor & soprano saxophone; Melissa Aldana (tenor saxophone); Linda May Han Oh (bass); Jeff "Tain" Watts (drums); TBA piano

This show is an ode to those hours required to achieve greatness—a tribute to the dedication necessary to realize physical ambitions and an acknowledgement that the backstory is often more spectacular than the finished product. 062e993d-d9a2-476b-a7bd-e5db6db0d18e: w/ Julian Lage, Asante Santi Debriano, and Will Calhoun An artist The Boston Globe accurately describes as “jazz royalty,” GRAMMY-winning saxophonist Joe Lovano showcases his latest ensemble for the second two nights of his 2026-27 Season residency — a masterful assemblage of virtuosos including guitar great Julian Lage, esteemed bassist Asante Santi Debriano, and Living Colour drummer Will Calhoun — performing music from Lovano’s new ECM Records release Paramount Quartet. Cutting his professional teeth with the bands of Woody Herman and Mel Lewis, Lovano is the most acclaimed saxophonist and composer in modern jazz, leading over 40 albums and forging long-term partnerships with John Scofield and Paul Motian and collaborating with artists ranging from Jim Hall and McCoy Tyner to Abbey Lincoln and Elvin Jones. The spark of the Paramount Quartet dates to a meeting with Debriano and Calhoun at a fundraiser for Puerto Rico hurricane relief in 2023 and adding Lage to the mix was a natural step, as the two had been talking about doing a project together for over two decades. Consisting of all original compositions and a loving version of Wayne Shorter’s “Lady Day,” the album is possessed of a singular magic. As Lovano himself puts it, “There's a lot of magic that just kind of unfolds as we play. And the more we play, the more magical it becomes." Personnel: Joe Lovano (tenor & soprano saxophone); Julian Lage (guitar); Asante Santi Debriano (bass); Will Calhoun (drums)

4fb779b7-bce1-443c-9215-e1f7dcdcb09c: Formed in 1985, the Ukulele Orchestra of Great Britain began as an unconventional ensemble exploring the expressive range of the ukulele in unexpected repertoire and settings. Performing initially in small venues, the group developed a distinctive approach that pairs formal presentation with playful musical exploration. More than four decades later, they continue to thrill audiences with offbeat humor and four-stringed virtuosity. With no drums, pianos, backing tracks, guitars, or electronic enhancement, the orchestra presents an astonishing palette of ukuleles and a menagerie of voices in a collision of post-punk performance and old classics.

The spark of the Paramount Quartet dates to a meeting with Debriano and Calhoun at a fundraiser for Puerto Rico hurricane relief in 2023 and adding Lage to the mix was a natural step, as the two had been talking about doing a project together for over two decades. Consisting of all original compositions and a loving version of Wayne Shorter’s “Lady Day,” the album is possessed of a singular magic. As Lovano himself puts it, “There's a lot of magic that just kind of unfolds as we play. And the more we play, the more magical it becomes." Personnel: Joe Lovano (tenor & soprano saxophone); Julian Lage (guitar); Asante Santi Debriano (bass); Will Calhoun (drums)

173afb3d-94dc-47ca-93f4-b43dc160e48a: This meditation and study group is based in the Insight Meditation tradition and its sources in Thai Forest and Burmese Theravāda Buddhism. To this foundation, we add exploration of Mahāyāna Dharmas particularly from the Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñāpāramitā) literature and lineage. The group meets weekly online, and on fourth Tuesdays live at the Alembic. The focus of the group is on deepening in Buddhist liberation practice, and exploring the links between individual & systemic liberation in the form of social justice and collective healing. I bring a particular focus on working with the nervous system and resolving the symptoms of trauma, supported by devotional practice, study, and ethics as the basis of the path. All are welcome. Cost is $5, plus Dāna (pay what you can). This is the online version of the event: https://momence.com/l/GBhB5e6w Sean Oakes, PhD (he/him, queer, of Spanish/Puerto Rican and Northern European ancestry living on unceded Pomo land in California), teaches Buddhism, Yoga, and somatic practice. He has studied in Theravāda, Zen, and Vajrāyāna Buddhist lineages since 1993, including training as a monk in Burma, and was authorized to teach Insight Meditation by Jack Kornfield in 2010. His primary Buddhist teachers include Kornfield, Sylvia Boorstein, Gil Fronsdal, Eugene Cash, Kittisaro, Ṭhānissara, Ṭhānissaro Bhikkhu, Anam Thubten, and Chammyay Sayadaw (U Janaka), with whom he ordained as a bhikkhu for a Rains Retreat in Burma in 2002. He studied Haṭha and Vinyāsa Yogas with Alice Joanou, Rachel Shaw, Amanda Moran, and David Moreno, and taught mindfulness-based āsana and prāṇāyāma for 10 years. He performed for many years in music, dance, and performance art, including with Keith Hennessy’s Circo Zero, and was certified in Somatic Experiencing (SE) and Organic Intelligence (OI) with Steven Hoskinson, integrating the complex systems approach from OI in a distinctively Buddhist approach to trauma resolution. He received his PhD in Performance Studies from UC Davis in 2016, writing on extraordinary states of consciousness in Buddhist meditation and experimental dance. He teaches at Spirit Rock Meditation Center, East Bay Meditation Center, Insight Timer, and elsewhere, focusing on the integration of philosophy, somatics, and social justice discourse with the Dharma. Website: SeanFeitOakes.com

dd8dbc78-e5ae-46ce-963c-81e815eeb1e3: A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli. Relatefulness is an exploration of what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. It is a close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, with slightly more emphasis on group interaction and flexibility in how to express what is arising in the present moment. This is a mixed-levels event. Beginners are welcome and will be supported with tools to aid their exploration. Advanced practitioners will be challenged to find the next edge of their practice. We cap attendance for the event at 15 people. If you want to be sure to be able to join, purchase your ticket in advance! What We’ll Explore Through paired, small group, and full group processes, we will practice: Noticing and naming the content of our experience, including: our emotions, body sensations, and present moment reactions to others in the group. Noticing and naming the context of our experience, including: our assumptions, the norms of the group, and projections onto one another and society. Revealing our experience to one another to help all of us see each other and our broader social reality more clearly. Leading the group in the direction we want to go. This is a practice where all participants are invited to notice their desires for the group and to practice directing the group by embodying the kinds of expression they want to see more of. Why Come? You may be looking to: Cultivate more authentic, nourishing relationships, where you can be yourself and stay connected. Take your insights about personal growth and explore them in an interpersonal context. Set clear, compassionate boundaries instead of repeating painful patterns This practice helps to develop skills that support all of the above. Also, it's fun! What Not to Expect This is not a therapy session or group healing experience, although healing can occur. It’s a group exploration of what is arising in the present moment. This naturally tends to bring out more truth and love in the group, but there is not a particular goal or endpoint we are trying to reach. Here’s what NOT to expect: A space free of conflict or triggers. When people are open about what's coming up in their experience, things can get edgy sometimes! We don’t view being triggered as inherently negative, but rather a natural part of the human experience that can be rich to explore. We aim for a space where safety grows from honesty and genuine care, not from avoiding interpersonal conflict. To support this, we will establish some boundaries up front, such as asking for explicit consent before making physical contact with others. No enforced hierarchy of emotions. Beauty, awkwardness, boredom, anger, and joy are all welcome. Each experience has worth, and none automatically justify themselves as more important. Expression without attunement. We value honest expression, and we also stay attentive to its impact on others. This is a space for mindful connection, not expression at any cost. Facilitators may pause or redirect moments that move away from relational presence. Other logistics and notes Participants enter the space at 6:30 and we close the doors for the event at 6:35. Please arrive on time! We hope to see you at a future event! Feel free to reach out to jhrosenberg [at] gmail [dot] com or dbricciardelli [at] gmail [dot] com if you have questions about whether this event is a fit for you. More about the facilitators Josh Rosenberg (he/him) is a certified facilitator through the Relateful Company training program. He has hosted and facilitated weekly relatefulness sessions for small groups for several years while continuing to grow his practice through retreats and regularly engaging other facilitators. Josh loves exploring what's honestly coming up in the present moment in a group of people, and the novelty and relief it tends to bring. When he's not leading relatefulness sessions or at work, you may find him loving the heck out of music, movies, and comedy, participating in Michael Taft's meditation courses, or passionately following the New York Jets football team despite its many flaws. In his day job, Josh is CEO at the Forecasting Research Institute, a nonprofit aiming to advance the science of forecasting and increase its policy-relevance. Daniel Ricciardelli (he/him) has hundreds of hours in relational awareness practices of various forms, and is a certified Relatefulness practitioner through the Relateful Company. He draws from a decade of experience guiding men’s circles, performance dance teams, applied AI research, and meditation. Some recent inspirations of his are Ego Development Theory, madhyamaka philosophy, and Brazilian zouk. He is known for his steady, compassionate presence and calibrated relational risk-taking. He works full-time at the intersection of mental health and AI as a machine learning researcher.

c49a169a-52f6-4a22-ba9e-d7b5bb523930: By increasing the flow of oxygen or Prana in our bodies, we can begin to move and release tension. In this class we shift our focus from the realm of thoughts to the intricate web of electrical signals within our bodies. Regardless of whether you've faced significant stress or trauma, this approach offers profound benefits to the nervous system. The accumulation of daily stressors can strain our bodies and without releasing this tension through expression, it can manifest as depression, anxiety, or disease over time. In this class we - Lay down for a guided short meditation. - Practice the breathwork sequence together for around 30 minutes. - Relax and recover. - Optional sharing and snacks afterwards. We have 26 trillion cells in our bodies and they all need oxygen. Come breathe with us and calibrate your nervous system! NOTE: Doors close 10 minutes after the start of class. This event is in-person only. Matt Barkin has been studying breathwork and meditation for over 15 years. His training is rooted in the ancient practices of Buddhist Vipassana and Kriya Yoga. His goal as a guide is to help students awaken their self-healing potential with the breath! Learn more about Matt here https://mattbarkin.com/breathwork/

b39e659f-b678-48b6-a9bd-a80a7704e249: with Pedrito Martínez Following his spectacular performance last season as part of Terence Blanchard’s UpSwing series, Cuban piano savant Alfredo Rodríguez returns with his powerful Afro-Cuban ensemble featuring the dynamic percussion master Pedrito Martínez for this evening of rhythmic fireworks. After Quincy Jones first heard Alfredo Rodríguez at the Monteux Jazz Festival in 2006 the legendary producer guided his ascent as Rodríguez became one of Cuba’s most visible and creatively unfettered musicians. Based in Los Angeles since he defected in 2009, the pianist has released a series of increasingly expansive albums for Mack Avenue, incorporating sounds from South India, Argentina, Spain, the Middle East and beyond. His formidable technique and soulful approach was described by the Mercury News as “the way Monk might have sounded if he had been born in Chick Corea’s body and raised on a diet of Bach, Chopin and Stravinsky in a Havana conservatory.” Released on his own Take Cover imprint, Rodriguez’s new album is a blistering collection of standards and covers called ¡Take Cover! that includes his takes on the music of Tito Puente, Henry Mancini, Stevie Wonder, The Eagles, Lalo Shifrin, and more. Personnel: Alfredo Rodríguez (piano); Pedrito Martínez (percussion); Others TBA

Did their friendships stand the test of time? Why do they remember certain moments from their past differently? From Pulitzer Prize–winning and two-time Tony Award–winning playwright Branden Jacob-Jenkins ( Gloria ) comes a new profound tragicomedy about the reunion that awaits us all.

5018ed97-4825-4e1f-8166-dcdb1be4c748: The final season installment of Terence Blanchard’s wildly popular UpSwing concert series highlights a pair of instrumentalists forging singular careers guided by uncompromising artistic vision. Los Angeles-based keyboardist and producer Julian Pollack, known widely as J3PO, is among the most exciting young artists on the scene. Raised in Berkeley, he was an award-winning member of the SFJAZZ High School All-Stars and appeared on Marian McPartland’s iconic Piano Jazz program on NPR at age 18. Since then, Pollack has emerged as a visionary force bridging jazz virtuosity with electronic production, hip-hop, and experimental sound design. He has worked with artists across jazz and contemporary music while developing a distinctive solo voice that positions him at the forefront of a new generation redefining jazz for the digital age. Vibraphonist Joel Ross has earned widespread renown as the most remarkable young voice on his instrument. Since the 2019 release of Ross’ debut album Kingmaker on Blue Note, he’s quickly established himself as a triple threat with a far-reaching approach. A graduate of Stockton’s University of the Pacific, Ross went on to study jazz at The New School and was mentored by former SFJAZZ Collective vibraphonist Stefon Harris. His new Blue Note release, Gospel Music, is a sonic interpretation of the Biblical story and an exploration of faith, featuring an expanded sextet lineup of his Good Vibes band. Personnel: J3PO; J3PO (keyboards); Others TBA; JOEL ROSS; Joel Ross (vibraphone); Others TBA
d46420ce-f981-45a3-beff-cb0f989639bf: Timeless Brazilian grooves with fresh arrangements and uplifting energy · The iconic sound of Sergio Mendes returns to the stage as Gracinha Leporace leads The Sergio Mendes Band in a spirited celebration of his life, joy, and musical legacy. Marking sixty years since the worldwide debut of Brasil ’66, this revitalized ensemble continues Mendes’ lifelong mission of sharing the vibrant rhythms and infectious soul of Brazilian music with audiences around the world. “Carrying Sergio’s music forward is both an honor and a responsibility,” said Gracinha Leporace. “This band embodies his spirit, joy, and deep love for Brazilian music. Sergio cherished every single member of this extraordinary ensemble, and we’re proud to continue what he started.” With a sound that blends timeless Brazilian grooves with fresh arrangements and uplifting energy, The Sergio Mendes Band brings a renewed sense of celebration to every performance. Each note pays tribute to Mendes’ remarkable inﬂuence — a career that helped shape the global appreciation of Bossa Nova, Samba, and the unmistakable warmth of Brazilian culture. About The Sergio Mendes Band The ensemble features: · Gracinha Leporace and Katie Hampton – Vocals · Leo Costa – Drums · Gibi dos Santos – Percussion · Kleber Jorge – Guitar & Vocals · Andre de Santanna – Bass · Scott Mayo – Keys, Saxophone, Flute & Vocals · Jamieson Trotter – Piano Together, the artists uphold Mendes’ vision of spreading joy through music — performing with the same passion, precision, and energy that captivated global audiences for over six decades. Continuing Legacy The Sergio Mendes Band invites long-term fans and new listeners alike to experience the sounds that deﬁned generations. Through their upcoming shows, they honor Sergio’s enduring message: that music has the power to unite, uplift, and bring people together from every part of the world.

1a0119e1-fcd0-45cc-8c26-0477f8194c6e: Sixteen-year-old Pi Patel sets out on a journey across the ocean with his family, only to find himself alone after a catastrophic shipwreck. Adrift on a lifeboat in the vast Pacific, he must learn to survive alongside a group of unlikely companions, including a hyena, a zebra, an orangutan, and a Bengal tiger. As the days stretch into weeks, reality and imagination begin to blur. Pi is pushed to his limits, confronting fear, faith, and the stories we tell ourselves to endure the unimaginable. Winner of five Olivier Awards including Best New Play, and hailed by The Guardian as “extraordinary and unmissable,” this breathtaking stage adaptation brings Yann Martel’s beloved novel to life through stunning visuals and groundbreaking puppetry. Life of Pi is a theatrical event about survival, belief, and the power of storytelling.

e01e1f0e-d655-48f8-b740-08fc23a43101: For over 30 years, Josh Davis has expressed his passion, taste, and values through the music he creates as DJ Shadow. The name alone evokes a high watermark for instrumental hip-hop and composition. From his first masterpiece Endtroducing…, to the genre-hopping UNKLE release Psyence Fiction, to the otherworldly elegance of The Private Press and its iconic single “Six Days,” to his underrated Bay Area celebration The Outsider, his work in the ‘90s and first decade of the 2000s is as essential as it is hard-to-pin-down. In the 2010s, Shadow released the sprawling The Less You Know, the Better, with its muscular forays into rock music, and closed the decade with The Mountain Will Fall and Our Pathetic Age, both very ambitious, risk-taking albums that boasted some of his best rap collaborations by working with Run the Jewels, Nas, and De La Soul, among others. If there’s a single red thread across this career, it's his restless ear, always searching to rescue some forgotten gem from the dustbin of music history or a fresh blast of sound from the cutting edge. It’s a practice Shadow learned as a young boy, enamored with collecting comic books, baseball cards, 12-inch records, and precious songs captured to cassette from the radio airwaves late at night in northern California. With great seriousness and love, he will describe the second-hand transistor AM radio on which he first heard Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five’s “The Message,” when he was 10 years old. Or his mind-expanding encounter with Public Enemy’s “Rebel Without a Pause” and that single’s howling saxophone blast. At the heart of DJ Shadow’s musical project is deep listening. “I’m always trying to please or impress the most advanced listener,” he says. The type of aficionado who will respect the layers upon layers of synth that went into making a sound that can’t be readily identified but will make you want to share the track with a friend and say, “This part right here.” The first sampled words heard on DJ Shadow’s forthcoming album Action Adventure, his seventh solo LP, are “all my records and tapes.” In fact, they are some of the only words heard on what is almost an entirely instrumental release; they’re a kind of thesis statement for an album that has its roots in the drifting, destabilizing days of the COVID lockdown. Action Adventure is an inward-looking project, made by Shadow alone without any collaborators. Action Adventure tells the listener: “This is about my relationship to music. My life as a collector and curator. All my records and tapes, and no one else’s.” The result is the most exciting DJ “Ozone Scraper” kicks off the album without preamble, just big, propulsive drums. It has the feeling of transportation, of jet engines lifting the passenger somewhere impossible. One of his favorites on Action Adventure, “Ozone Scraper” is an invitation to strap in and also sets the table for the kind of deep listening Shadow loves. The advanced listeners will marvel at the kind of “special effects,” as Shadow puts it, that went into creating the elusive synth noises. Like a child marveling at a summer blockbuster, you wonder: How did he do this? “You Played Me” is a miracle that happened by pure chance. Inspired by the eBay tapes, Shadow created a beat that had the crackling percussion and burbling synths of classic ‘80s R&B, like a lost René and Angela hit. “I loaded up the instrumental and looped it on my computer to play forever,” he explains. Then he started auditioning records in his collection that he hadn’t processed yet—an experiment to find the vocal in the haystack. “I dropped the needle on an acapella of a really obscure R&B 12-inch from around ‘84, ‘85 and I thought, ‘That actually works.’” Still, he wasn’t entirely sure, and he sent the song to his label as a reference for a potential collaboration… whoever it was needed to have this sound, Shadow told them. After a few weeks, though, he realized he already had what he needed—the acapella was correct. “It's an example of one of my favorite aspects of the music I make, which is just 100% serendipity,” he says. “There are a thousand records sitting next to me that aren't going to work; the right record got put on at the right moment to change the course of my album. It’s one of my favorite songs I’ve ever made.” The album has a cinematic quality, especially in its sequencing. The last quarter, from “Fleeting Youth” through “Reflecting Pool” and “Forever Changed,” is as cathartic as a well-told story, and ends on a triumphant note, with “She’s Evolving.” The oldest recording on Action Adventure, it’s another happy accident that nearly didn’t make the album. Initially Shadow doubted including a song from the cursed early days of lockdown and planned to end the album with a much sadder track. But it didn’t sit right and he kept returning to “She’s Evolving”—until it stuck. The title Action Adventure evokes the halcyon days of video store browsing, and it’s fitting that shadow LP in years. In March 2020, Shadow narrowly escaped from the European tour for his double-disc release Our Pathetic Age, landing back home in the Bay Area as the world shuttered. He watched his two teenage daughters endure homeschooling and tried to process his own emotions about the tour cut short; an album he was proud of that didn’t get to have its moment in public. “It was a very intense time,” he recalls. For over a year, he couldn’t imagine making any new music, or even listening to any contemporary music. “It was as if the music coming out was somehow tainted by the craziness we were living through, the chaos and upheaval. I needed to temporarily wallow in a bit of nostalgia, and not necessarily songs I knew”—but music from a time period that felt less fraught. Around this same time, in 2021, a friend directed Shadow to an eBay auction of about 200 tapes that were recorded off the radio from a mix station that serviced the Baltimore-D.C. area in the ‘80s. During that time, he taped Bay Area radio mixes and was able to get his hands on New York mixes as well, but these mixes felt entirely unique in their blend of dance music, R&B, and early hip-hop. They had a youthful, “we know no limits” quality that invigorated Shadow at a time when he desperately needed it. Shadow began work on Action Adventure on January 1, 2022, and the early tracks pushed him further into his compositional bag. “I didn't want to write music that was formatted for vocalists. I wanted to write music that flexed different energies,” he says. Though he isn’t classically trained, he asked himself questions like “which chord progression would be most natural here, and which would be least predictable?” and worked according to the inner logic that felt right to him. His rule for the record was simple: no compromises. “I’m entering my fourth decade doing this—what do I want to represent? I know that I don’t want to only make beats for some potential vocalist that I’ve never met, and who may not share my vision. I want this record to stand or fall on my own credentials.”

3811ae0d-3267-49c0-b175-192a97ec0c55: 5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic. In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing. 5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you. The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives. In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach. Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

b2eabf55-8a5f-41ce-9fde-81f452fc14fc: Many of us work with psychedelics without a guide or with limited support to integrate these experiences. That can feel painful or lonely when we’ve had meaningful journeys (and also when we’ve had disappointing journeys!). Healing – especially from interpersonal injuries – deepens when done in community. The same is true of personal and spiritual growth. Even the most joyful experiences are best metabolized when witnessed. Together, we become a mosaic – a colorful and varied community, greater together than the sum of our parts. Mosaic is a psychedelic integration circle for self-identified women. Here, you’ll find a supportive space to integrate the lessons, challenges, and wisdom from psychedelic journeys so that you can apply those learnings to everyday life. Together, we’ll seek to understand our psychedelic experiences and make profound insights accessible and actionable. Please arrive 10 minutes early to get settled in. We’ll begin promptly at the scheduled start time and cannot accommodate late arrivals. Thank you for helping us create a smooth experience for everyone. This is a drop-in, monthly supported peer group rather than a psychotherapy group. We create space for sharing stories and experiences, receiving support, and forging genuine connections. Meditation, mindful movement, somatic practices, Internal Family Systems parts work, and creative tools are all part of the fun. Whether you’re new to integration or looking to deepen your practice, you’ll find a supportive community here. Note: You’re invited to bring an object for our community altar that represents some aspect of your journey. No one turned away for lack of funds. If this applies to you, please pay at the door. This event is a closed container. There will be no further entry after 2:15. Dr. Lyssa Menard is a psychologist, psychedelic therapist, and professor (Northwestern University Medical School) with specialties in Integrative Medicine, trauma treatment, and health psychology. She is the founder of Strategies for Change, a coaching and consulting firm promoting personal, organizational, and leadership change and has been a consultant to a wide range of media outlets, including CNN, New York Times, and WebMD. She brings this varied background to her integration groups, facilitating growth and change through a multi-media concoction of integrative therapeutic approaches (mindful movement, creative arts, somatic healing and embodiment, social connection, and spiritual ritual). Dr. Menard’s book, "Results May Vary: Hope & Healing through Psychedelic-assisted Psychotherapy" is scheduled for release in 2026. As a beneficiary of excellent (and also, sadly, lackluster) psychedelic treatment, she is a skeptic of the field, a critic when necessary, and a true believer in the healing possibilities offered by these medicines. She serves as an advocate for community and patient education and fights for legal access to psychedelics for health and healing. As a recent transplant to California's Bay Area, Dr. Menard spends a ridiculous amount of time at The Berkeley Alembic, cavorting in nature, worshipping the sun, and developing community. Learn more about Lyssa here: https://lyssamenard.com/ Read Lyssa’s musings on Substack: https://lyssamenard.substack.com/
b4106019-39e3-472d-92cc-0de2414f56e4: Lucas and Arthur Jussen are among the leading piano duos performing today, appearing with orchestras including the Berlin Philharmonic and Boston Symphony and recording exclusively for Deutsche Grammophon. Their energetic, almost symbiotic playing has exhilarated audiences worldwide and earned them an Edison Klassiek Audience Award. This concert includes two-piano and four-hand rarities by Mendelssohn, Schubert, and Milhaud, as well as adaptations of colossal 20th-century orchestral touchstones: Ravel’s La valse and Stravinsky’s The Rite of Spring.

c7a51d7e-05fe-441d-b383-3b48f829219b: Winner of the 2019 American Pianists Award and finalist in the 2011 Thelonious Monk International Piano Competition, virtuoso Emmet Cohen is among the most acclaimed pianists in jazz, known widely as a member of bass great Christian McBride’s Tip City and music director with vocal phenom Veronica Swift, along with his stellar work as a bandleader. He steps back on the Miner stage with his working quintet after his sold-out 2026 performance focused on the music of Miles Davis and John Coltrane in honor of their centennials. The prodigious pianist started piano studies at three and released his 2011 debut In the Element while still enrolled at University of Florida’s Frost School of Music. He has accumulated nearly 20 major awards and honors over his career and created the acclaimed Masters Legacy Series of recordings and interviews in 2016 featuring collaboration with Ron Carter, Benny Golson, Albert “Tootie” Heath, George Coleman, and Houston Person. Cohen has been a member of the bands led by drumming luminaries Herlin Riley and Ali Jackson and hosted the wildly popular YouTube series Live From Emmet’s Place with a procession of special guests. Cohen has led 12 albums including his newest Mack Avenue release, 2024’s Vibe Provider. Personnel: Emmet Cohen (piano); Others TBA

7adc0295-7954-4cf7-8d43-8a79013a1529: Psychedelics can surface anything, including awe, insight, grief, trauma, even ancestral or collective pain. Without support, it can be hard to make sense of what happened, let alone carry it forward in a meaningful way. Yirah—often translated as awe, reverence, or a kind of holy trembling—is the feeling of standing at the edge of something vast, meaningful, and not entirely knowable. Psychedelic experiences often bring us right to that edge. This Jewish psychedelic integration circle offers a space to meet those moments together, within the safety of Jewish community and the container of Jewish teachings. Together, we make meaning of what we’ve seen and felt, and begin the slow, human work of weaving those insights into our lives. Please arrive 10 minutes early to get settled in. We’ll begin promptly at the scheduled start time and cannot accommodate late arrivals. Thank you for helping us create a smooth experience for everyone. Each monthly, drop-in circle includes grounding and intention-setting, a brief orientation, an experiential practice (meditation, movement, somatic work, or parts work), and small- and large-group sharing. This is a supported peer group rather than psychotherapy, designed to foster connection, reflection, and practical integration. Note: This is an affinity space exclusively for people who identify as Jewish—by heritage or conversion—including those who are part-Jewish. Those who do not meet these criteria will not be admitted. To support safety and connection in a time of deep division, we also hold a clear and intentional container: we do not engage in political discussion here. The focus is on integration, presence, and community. Whether you’re new to Jewish practice or finding your way back in, whether your journeys have been expansive, messy, or disorienting—you’re welcome here. Facilitator Bio: Lyssa Menard, PhD, is a clinical psychologist, psychedelic therapist, and professor at Northwestern University Medical School who specializes in trauma, integrative medicine, and what it actually takes to change. She’s been featured in places like CNN and The New York Times, but her real work happens in circles like this one—where people show up as they are and do the brave, uncomfortable, life-changing work of integration. Jewish by birth and in a more recent, intentional deep dive into Jewish life, Lyssa brings a deep respect for tradition alongside a willingness to question, wrestle, and reinterpret—in the long Jewish tradition of meaning-making. After all, Israel can be translated as “one who wrestles with God.” Her relationship to psychedelics is both professional and personal. She’s experienced their power, their limitations, and everything in between—which makes her equal parts skeptic and believer.

2d660701-99de-4493-836b-6238a95b7305: Topic and guest to be announced. The Chalice is a recurring psychedelic salon held at the Berkeley Alembic the first Wednesday of every month. Instead of the mainstream focus on clinical trials, legal frameworks, and psychotherapy, the Chalice will draw from the deeper humanistic wells of history, poetry, the gods, ethnobotany, humor, and mystery. We are less interested in fetishizing psychedelic substances or psychedelic experiences than in cultivating psychedelic culture and exploring what it means to be psychedelic people. This first half of this event will be streamed online. The co-hosts for Chalice are Erik Davis, author and Alembic co-founder; Maria Mangini, co-founder of the Women’s Visionary Council and old-school head; and Christian Greer, currently a lecturer on counterculture at Stanford University. The first half of each gathering will feature a talk or special guest interview; the second half of the evening is designed to develop the community, sometimes with breakout groups, story hours, and peer-to-peer discussion, and always with more questions than answers. J. Christian Greer, PhD, is a scholar of Religious Studies with a special focus on global psychedelic culture. He has held teaching positions at Harvard University, Yale University, and is currently a lecturer at Stanford's Medical School. He is the co-founder, and the co-chair of the Drugs and Religion program unit at the American Academy of Religion, and each June, he leads “The Psychedelic Universe: Global Perspectives on Higher Consciousness,” an intensive, 2-week seminar on the history of psychedelics, hosted on-location at the University of Amsterdam, Netherlands. Alongside his research, he is an organizer for the Order of St. George's Horse, a pilgrimage confraternity & book publisher. His latest books include, Void Machines: the Paper Shrines of J. Christian Greer is a collection of his artwork, and Kumano Kodo: Pilgrimage to Powerspots (co-authored with Dr. Michelle Oing) which analyzes the pilgrimage folklore associated with the rainforests of Japan's Kii Peninsula. Learn more about his work here: orderofstgeorgeshorse.com Erik Davis, PhD, is an author, award-winning journalist, and teacher based in San Francisco. His wide-ranging work focuses on alternative religion, media culture, the popular imagination, and the psychedelic underground. He is the author of High Weirdness: Drugs, Esoterica, and Visionary Experience in the Seventies (2019); Nomad Codes: Adventures in Modern Esoterica (2010); The Visionary State: A Journey through California’s Spiritual Landscape (2006), a critical volume on Led Zeppelin (2005), and the celebrated cult classic TechGnosis: Myth, Magic, and Mysticism in the Age of Information (1998), which remains in print. Davis’s scholarly and popular essays on music, technoculture, drugs, and spirituality have appeared in scores of books, magazines, and journals, and his writing has been translated into a dozen languages. Davis has spoken widely at universities, conferences, retreat centers, and festivals, and has been interviewed by CNN, the BBC, NPR, and the New York Times. He graduated from Yale University in 1988, and earned his PhD in religious studies at Rice University in 2015. He writes the online publication the Burning Shore (www.burningshore.com), and his next book is Blotter: the Untold Story of an Acid Medium (2024).www.techgnosis.com Mariavittoria Mangini, PhD, FNP has written extensively on the impact of psychedelic experiences in shaping the lives of her contemporaries, and has worked closely with many of the most distinguished investigators in this field. She is one of the founders of the Women’s Visionary Council, a nonprofit organization that supports investigations into non-ordinary forms of consciousness and organizes gatherings of researchers, healers, artists, and activists whose work explores these states. She is a visiting scholar at the Berkeley Center for the Science of Psychedelics, and Professor Emerita in the School of Science, Allied Health, and Nursing at Holy Names University. For the last 50 years, she has been a part of the Hog Farm, a well-known communal family based in Berkeley and in Laytonville, California.

d6bdf68a-79d2-4f7f-bef0-af2fbbb20490: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

1ebf6217-3408-41b5-a363-4750ea75e4c1: A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli. Relatefulness is an exploration of what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. It is a close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, with slightly more emphasis on group interaction and flexibility in how to express what is arising in the present moment. This is a mixed-levels event. Beginners are welcome and will be supported with tools to aid their exploration. Advanced practitioners will be challenged to find the next edge of their practice. We cap attendance for the event at 15 people. If you want to be sure to be able to join, purchase your ticket in advance! What We’ll Explore Through paired, small group, and full group processes, we will practice: Noticing and naming the content of our experience, including: our emotions, body sensations, and present moment reactions to others in the group. Noticing and naming the context of our experience, including: our assumptions, the norms of the group, and projections onto one another and society. Revealing our experience to one another to help all of us see each other and our broader social reality more clearly. Leading the group in the direction we want to go. This is a practice where all participants are invited to notice their desires for the group and to practice directing the group by embodying the kinds of expression they want to see more of. Why Come? You may be looking to: Cultivate more authentic, nourishing relationships, where you can be yourself and stay connected. Take your insights about personal growth and explore them in an interpersonal context. Set clear, compassionate boundaries instead of repeating painful patterns This practice helps to develop skills that support all of the above. Also, it's fun! What Not to Expect This is not a therapy session or group healing experience, although healing can occur. It’s a group exploration of what is arising in the present moment. This naturally tends to bring out more truth and love in the group, but there is not a particular goal or endpoint we are trying to reach. Here’s what NOT to expect: A space free of conflict or triggers. When people are open about what's coming up in their experience, things can get edgy sometimes! We don’t view being triggered as inherently negative, but rather a natural part of the human experience that can be rich to explore. We aim for a space where safety grows from honesty and genuine care, not from avoiding interpersonal conflict. To support this, we will establish some boundaries up front, such as asking for explicit consent before making physical contact with others. No enforced hierarchy of emotions. Beauty, awkwardness, boredom, anger, and joy are all welcome. Each experience has worth, and none automatically justify themselves as more important. Expression without attunement. We value honest expression, and we also stay attentive to its impact on others. This is a space for mindful connection, not expression at any cost. Facilitators may pause or redirect moments that move away from relational presence. Other logistics and notes Participants enter the space at 6:30 and we close the doors for the event at 6:35. Please arrive on time! We hope to see you at a future event! Feel free to reach out to jhrosenberg [at] gmail [dot] com or dbricciardelli [at] gmail [dot] com if you have questions about whether this event is a fit for you. More about the facilitators Josh Rosenberg (he/him) is a certified facilitator through the Relateful Company training program. He has hosted and facilitated weekly relatefulness sessions for small groups for several years while continuing to grow his practice through retreats and regularly engaging other facilitators. Josh loves exploring what's honestly coming up in the present moment in a group of people, and the novelty and relief it tends to bring. When he's not leading relatefulness sessions or at work, you may find him loving the heck out of music, movies, and comedy, participating in Michael Taft's meditation courses, or passionately following the New York Jets football team despite its many flaws. In his day job, Josh is CEO at the Forecasting Research Institute, a nonprofit aiming to advance the science of forecasting and increase its policy-relevance. Daniel Ricciardelli (he/him) has hundreds of hours in relational awareness practices of various forms, and is a certified Relatefulness practitioner through the Relateful Company. He draws from a decade of experience guiding men’s circles, performance dance teams, applied AI research, and meditation. Some recent inspirations of his are Ego Development Theory, madhyamaka philosophy, and Brazilian zouk. He is known for his steady, compassionate presence and calibrated relational risk-taking. He works full-time at the intersection of mental health and AI as a machine learning researcher.

bcabe3b1-32dc-4984-843f-f3086f20c74a: The inspired collaboration between Snarky Puppy guitarist Mark Lettieri and the virtuosic Indian sitar master Purbayan Chatterjee comes to the Miner Auditorium stage for one night, highlighting their shared spirit of exploration, improvisational telepathy, and quicksilver dexterity. They bring a night of spirited musical dialog, performing compositions from their 2026 GroundUP Music debut, Feathered Creatures, and more than a few surprises. Mark Lettieri, renowned for his work with Snarky Puppy and The Fearless Flyers, has become one of contemporary instrumental music’s most inventive guitar voices. Raised in the Bay Area and seasoned in the Dallas music scene, Lettieri developed a style that merges funk precision, jazz sophistication, and rock intensity. A multi-GRAMMY winner with Snarky Puppy and a GRAMMY nominee for his solo release Deep: The Baritone Sessions, Vol. 2, he is celebrated for groove-driven compositions and fearless improvisation. Purbayan Chatterjee stands among India’s foremost sitar maestros, carrying forward the Senia Maihar gharana tradition while expanding it into contemporary global music. Trained by legendary masters and honored with the Rashtrapati Award as a teenage prodigy, Chatterjee has built an international reputation through dazzling technique, emotional depth, and cross-cultural collaborations, as on his all-star 2021 album Unbounded featuring the late Zakir Hussain, drummer Antonio Sánchez, and Snarky Puppy leader Michael League. Lettieri and Chatterjee’s new album Feathered Creatures promises a vivid meeting of rhythmic fire, lyrical beauty, and boundary-defying musical conversation. Personnel: Mark Lettieri (guitar); Purbayan Chatterjee (sitar)

381e537e-2032-4551-b095-22a19e971655: The piano trio has been one of the most durable, beloved, and flexible formats in jazz history. Manchester-based GoGo Penguin turns this most venerable construct on its ear, infusing direct influences from contemporary electronic music and modern classical concepts into their singular ensemble approach that has earned well-deserved raves from all corners of the music world. The band’s hypnotic, swirling grooves are acoustic adaptations of pieces composed with sequencing software, and rely as much on additive development and dynamic contrasts as improvisation, with pianist Chris Illingsworth’s powerful melodic statements anchored by Nick Blacka’s thunderous bass and the skittering break-beat rhythms of drummer Jon Scott. The strength of their first two independent albums and magnetic live performances led to inclusion on Rolling Stone’s list of “20 Great New British Artists to Watch,” as well as a deal with Blue Note Records, who released their 2016 breakout, Man Made Object. Fast forward to the present — the band are riding high from their eighth release, the 2025 XXIM Records album Necessary Fictions, which integrates a wider sonic spectrum through modular synthesizers, and have recently released the follow-up Call to the Void, a three-track EP that dives still deeper into electronic experimentation. Pushing the jazz trio form in unprecedented new directions, GoGo Penguin truly sounds like nothing else on Earth. Personnel: Chris Illingsworth (piano); Nick Blacka (bass); Jon Scott (drums)

029d50a3-5858-46fb-a6e9-c730345d92a8: Creative expression is a way to integrate phenomenon and visions experienced in altered states of consciousness, whether they be meditative or entheogenic in nature. From the very first forms of mark-making to the caves of Lascaux to the works of Pablo Amaringo and Alex Grey, humanity has sought to understand our internal landscapes through visual expression. Alligator Lizards in the Air: Healing and Integration through Creative Expression, is a once a month chance to bring these experiences to life through two dimensional mark making. Art mediums from paint to colored pencils, crayons to markers, will be available for everyone to use along with paper and canvas. Krisztina Lazar will be your visionary guide in creativity and will help you realize your experience before your eyes. No art background needed for this class. All you need is an open mind and a willingness to explore. No one turned away for lack of funds. If this applies to you, please email hello@berkeleyalembic.org at least 48 hours before the event start. Krisztina Lazar is a visionary artist primarily working in oil paint, watercolor and drawing. She is a Mische Technique lineage holder, a mixture of oil and egg tempera painting invented during the Dutch Renaissance and revolutionized by modern master, Ernst Fuchs. This technique creates an opalescent under painting that the colors are then glazed over, rendering each painting out of light rather than shadow, bringing the images to life with fractal clarity. Utilizing this transformative style that she learned from visionary pioneer, Brigid Marlin, her current body of work explores painting a hybrid of Mische and Alla Prima to render hyperealistic sacred art. With these two techniques combined, Krisztina creates images of Pop Shamanism, portals and visions that speak to today’s cultural climate of the occult, magic, fantasy, psychedelics, meditation, pop, nostalgia, and the environment movement. Originally from Cleveland, OH, she completed her BFA at Carnegie Mellon University in 2004 and her MFA graduate degree in 2011 at the San Francisco Art Institute New Genres department. Her paintings have been exhibited in group and solo shows throughout the United States and Europe, most notably at the H.R. Geiger museum in Gruyere, Switzerland. She teaches her unique styles of painting to many students in group and private settings. Her work has been featured in multiple articles, galleries and book publications. She currently lives and works in Northern California.

2454eee3-076d-4d9d-b8cb-4879d65f3a42: 5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic. In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing. 5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you. The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives. In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach. Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

cfa4be27-ea14-4316-9870-75b6bc6cb7cb: A pair of master musicians representing the diversity of string instrument traditions, Derek Gripper and Alam Khan unite for a project that dissolves musical borders and reimagines the possibilities of global acoustic music. Gripper has earned international acclaim for his groundbreaking adaptations of West African kora music for solo guitar, a feat that led legendary kora master Toumani Diabaté to remark that Gripper had “taken the guitar to a new place.” His work bridges African classical traditions with jazz and contemporary composition, establishing him as one of the world’s most innovative guitarists. Alam Khan, the son of the legendary sarod maestro Ali Akbar Khan, carries forward one of India’s most revered musical lineages. A master of the sarod and a gifted composer, Khan blends the rigor of Hindustani classical music with adventurous cross-cultural collaboration, earning respect across both traditional and contemporary music circles. Together, Gripper and Khan engage in a transcendent musical conversation—an immersive journey through African, Indian, and contemporary sound worlds shaped by improvisation, technical brilliance, and deep cultural exchange. Personnel: Derek Gripper (guitar); Alam Khan (sarod)

56addc99-ce04-4346-b1ef-a0f718922435: Few artists embody the pulse of Latin jazz like Poncho Sánchez, a conguero whose hands seem to translate history into rhythm. He makes his first appearance at the SFJAZZ Center with this performance, joined by the latest iteration of his Latin Band. Born in Texas and raised in Southern California, Sánchez emerged from a rich blend of Afro-Cuban traditions and bebop influences, eventually becoming one of the most influential percussionists in jazz. His early mentorship under vibraphonist Cal Tjader positioned him at the heart of a lineage that includes giants like Tito Puente and Mongo Santamaría—artists who helped define the genre he now carries forward. With his band, Sánchez forged a sound that is both scholarly and electrifying: tight horn lines, driving congas, and an irresistible groove that merges jazz sophistication with street-level soul. Over decades and more than 20 albums, he has transformed Latin jazz into a living, evolving conversation, earning a GRAMMY and global acclaim. His latest project, Poncho Sánchez & His Latin Jazz Band Live at the Belly Up Tavern, captures that vitality in real time. The album delivers fresh arrangements and the kinetic energy of a live performance, proving that Sánchez’s music is not archival—it is alive, urgent, and still expanding. In every strike of the drum, Poncho Sánchez doesn’t just play Latin jazz—he sustains its heartbeat. Personnel: Poncho Sánchez (congas); Others TBA

ebcf6667-265f-46c5-8215-d54aa8091163: This meditation and study group is based in the Insight Meditation tradition and its sources in Thai Forest and Burmese Theravāda Buddhism. To this foundation, we add exploration of Mahāyāna Dharmas particularly from the Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñāpāramitā) literature and lineage. The group meets weekly online, and on fourth Tuesdays live at the Alembic. The focus of the group is on deepening in Buddhist liberation practice, and exploring the links between individual & systemic liberation in the form of social justice and collective healing. I bring a particular focus on working with the nervous system and resolving the symptoms of trauma, supported by devotional practice, study, and ethics as the basis of the path. All are welcome. Cost is $5, plus Dāna (pay what you can). This is the online version of the event: https://momence.com/l/GBhB5e6w Sean Oakes, PhD (he/him, queer, of Spanish/Puerto Rican and Northern European ancestry living on unceded Pomo land in California), teaches Buddhism, Yoga, and somatic practice. He has studied in Theravāda, Zen, and Vajrāyāna Buddhist lineages since 1993, including training as a monk in Burma, and was authorized to teach Insight Meditation by Jack Kornfield in 2010. His primary Buddhist teachers include Kornfield, Sylvia Boorstein, Gil Fronsdal, Eugene Cash, Kittisaro, Ṭhānissara, Ṭhānissaro Bhikkhu, Anam Thubten, and Chammyay Sayadaw (U Janaka), with whom he ordained as a bhikkhu for a Rains Retreat in Burma in 2002. He studied Haṭha and Vinyāsa Yogas with Alice Joanou, Rachel Shaw, Amanda Moran, and David Moreno, and taught mindfulness-based āsana and prāṇāyāma for 10 years. He performed for many years in music, dance, and performance art, including with Keith Hennessy’s Circo Zero, and was certified in Somatic Experiencing (SE) and Organic Intelligence (OI) with Steven Hoskinson, integrating the complex systems approach from OI in a distinctively Buddhist approach to trauma resolution. He received his PhD in Performance Studies from UC Davis in 2016, writing on extraordinary states of consciousness in Buddhist meditation and experimental dance. He teaches at Spirit Rock Meditation Center, East Bay Meditation Center, Insight Timer, and elsewhere, focusing on the integration of philosophy, somatics, and social justice discourse with the Dharma. Website: SeanFeitOakes.com

69d289b3-c3da-48e8-8f07-03ff9e3f07df: A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli. Relatefulness is an exploration of what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. It is a close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, with slightly more emphasis on group interaction and flexibility in how to express what is arising in the present moment. This is a mixed-levels event. Beginners are welcome and will be supported with tools to aid their exploration. Advanced practitioners will be challenged to find the next edge of their practice. We cap attendance for the event at 15 people. If you want to be sure to be able to join, purchase your ticket in advance! What We’ll Explore Through paired, small group, and full group processes, we will practice: Noticing and naming the content of our experience, including: our emotions, body sensations, and present moment reactions to others in the group. Noticing and naming the context of our experience, including: our assumptions, the norms of the group, and projections onto one another and society. Revealing our experience to one another to help all of us see each other and our broader social reality more clearly. Leading the group in the direction we want to go. This is a practice where all participants are invited to notice their desires for the group and to practice directing the group by embodying the kinds of expression they want to see more of. Why Come? You may be looking to: Cultivate more authentic, nourishing relationships, where you can be yourself and stay connected. Take your insights about personal growth and explore them in an interpersonal context. Set clear, compassionate boundaries instead of repeating painful patterns This practice helps to develop skills that support all of the above. Also, it's fun! What Not to Expect This is not a therapy session or group healing experience, although healing can occur. It’s a group exploration of what is arising in the present moment. This naturally tends to bring out more truth and love in the group, but there is not a particular goal or endpoint we are trying to reach. Here’s what NOT to expect: A space free of conflict or triggers. When people are open about what's coming up in their experience, things can get edgy sometimes! We don’t view being triggered as inherently negative, but rather a natural part of the human experience that can be rich to explore. We aim for a space where safety grows from honesty and genuine care, not from avoiding interpersonal conflict. To support this, we will establish some boundaries up front, such as asking for explicit consent before making physical contact with others. No enforced hierarchy of emotions. Beauty, awkwardness, boredom, anger, and joy are all welcome. Each experience has worth, and none automatically justify themselves as more important. Expression without attunement. We value honest expression, and we also stay attentive to its impact on others. This is a space for mindful connection, not expression at any cost. Facilitators may pause or redirect moments that move away from relational presence. Other logistics and notes Participants enter the space at 6:30 and we close the doors for the event at 6:35. Please arrive on time! We hope to see you at a future event! Feel free to reach out to jhrosenberg [at] gmail [dot] com or dbricciardelli [at] gmail [dot] com if you have questions about whether this event is a fit for you. More about the facilitators Josh Rosenberg (he/him) is a certified facilitator through the Relateful Company training program. He has hosted and facilitated weekly relatefulness sessions for small groups for several years while continuing to grow his practice through retreats and regularly engaging other facilitators. Josh loves exploring what's honestly coming up in the present moment in a group of people, and the novelty and relief it tends to bring. When he's not leading relatefulness sessions or at work, you may find him loving the heck out of music, movies, and comedy, participating in Michael Taft's meditation courses, or passionately following the New York Jets football team despite its many flaws. In his day job, Josh is CEO at the Forecasting Research Institute, a nonprofit aiming to advance the science of forecasting and increase its policy-relevance. Daniel Ricciardelli (he/him) has hundreds of hours in relational awareness practices of various forms, and is a certified Relatefulness practitioner through the Relateful Company. He draws from a decade of experience guiding men’s circles, performance dance teams, applied AI research, and meditation. Some recent inspirations of his are Ego Development Theory, madhyamaka philosophy, and Brazilian zouk. He is known for his steady, compassionate presence and calibrated relational risk-taking. He works full-time at the intersection of mental health and AI as a machine learning researcher.

59a9a25d-f429-447a-a8e2-80a66b376711: By increasing the flow of oxygen or Prana in our bodies, we can begin to move and release tension. In this class we shift our focus from the realm of thoughts to the intricate web of electrical signals within our bodies. The accumulation of daily stressors can strain our bodies and without releasing this tension through expression, it can manifest as depression, anxiety, or disease over time. In this class we - Lay down for a guided short meditation. - Practice the breathwork sequence together for around 30 minutes. - Relax and recover. - Optional sharing and snacks afterwards. This event is in-person only. Matt Barkin has been studying breathwork and meditation for over 15 years. His training is rooted in the ancient practices of Buddhist Vipassana and Kriya Yoga. b9f0e5df-480f-489f-8212-0ba45d3975e6: The most influential figure in modern Afro-Cuban jazz for more than half a century, virtuoso pianist, composer and arranger Chucho Valdés celebrates his 85th Birthday with this week of special concerts. The son of Cuban pianist Bebo Valdés, the winner of seven GRAMMYs and seven Latin GRAMMY Awards joined Armando Romeu’s celebrated Cuban Orchestra of Modern Music in 1967, a time when the communist government still considered American jazz anti-revolutionary. He was already recognized as the most formidable pianist of his generation when he launched Irakere in 1973 with a phenomenal cast that included saxophonist Paquito D’Rivera and trumpeter Arturo Sandoval. Over the ensuing years, Valdés has concentrated on his career as a solo artist, recording over 25 albums and co-writing the landmark 2018 book Decoding Afro-Cuban Jazz in collaboration with SFJAZZ Director of Education Rebeca Mauleón. His staggering legacy was summed up by the Boston Globe, who lauded him for “an encyclopedic vocabulary of Afro-Cuban rhythms and an expansive palette that includes all manner of modern jazz as well as traditional classical repertoire.” Most recently, Valdés has brought his Afro-Cuban Messengers, Irakere 50, and Royal Quartet projects to SFJAZZ, and for this 85th birthday celebration event, Valdés will be joined by a superlative lineup of musicians and special guests, ending the 2026-27 Season in grand fashion. Personnel: Chucho Valdés (piano); Others TBA

Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between.
